items.title: docs: refresh README — real throughput numbers, mechanism, multi-GPU loading, tuning
items.body:
## What

README refresh. The headline claimed **"up to 25Gbps"** (~3 GB/s) — underselling the repo's *own* benchmark chart (~18 GB/s) by ~6x, most likely a bits/bytes mix-up — and nothing shipped since 2025-11 was documented: not the v0.3 parallel reader, not the v0.4.1 sharded distributed read.

### Changes

- **Headline** → *"Disk-to-GPU tensor loading at up to 18 GB/s — no GDS required"*, directly supported by the existing `scripts/run_benchmark.py` chart below it.
- **New "Production numbers" section** — true-cold fleet measurements (H100 fleet, network-backed weight store, bit-verified loads): 15.35 GB in 12.5 s and 25.41 GB in 18 s vs 255/245 s for the fault-driven mmap walk (14–20x). New light/dark chart (`media/coldstart-{black,white}.png`) with data + provenance committed in `scripts/plot_fleet_coldstart.py`. Clearly labeled as fal fleet measurements, with the three-tier table (hot 10–18 GB/s / node-warm 5–12 GB/s / true-cold 14–20x).
- **New "How it works"** — macroblock layout, 16 preadv threads with per-thread pinned buffers + CUDA streams, mincore-gated O_DIRECT, zero-copy reconstruction, and the "GDS without the deployment pain" positioning.
- **New "Multi-GPU loading"** — documents `read_flashpack_file_distributed` and `sharded=True` (v0.4.1), with the 8xH200 numbers from the constants.py sweeps (14.5 GB pack in ~0.65 s; 12.9 GB replicated in ~32–37 ms depending on strategy).
- **New "Installation"** and **"Tuning"** (all main `FLASHPACK_*` env vars with verified defaults).
- **Updates section** backfilled with v0.3.0/0.3.1, v0.4.0, v0.4.1 entries (dates match tags).
- Fixes: `FlashPackDiffusionPipeline` typo in the mixin example; `pack_to_file` sample was missing its required `target_dtype` argument (crashed on copy-paste); un-rendered backticks inside the HTML image captions; heading hierarchy (`# Integration Guide`/`# CLI Commands` now nest correctly in GitHub's outline).

### Verification

Every technical claim was checked against `src/` (env-var defaults and semantics — including the `FLASHPACK_READ_CHUNK_BYTES` 64 MiB default, which differs from `constants.py`'s unrelated 4 MiB write-path constant — distributed API signature/behavior, mincore gate), and every number against its measurement source (repo benchmark charts, constants.py sweep comments, fal fleet A/B records). `uvx prek run --all-files` is green.

items.body:
## Overview

Updates the README to match the recently-updated wording on [blerpc.net](https://blerpc.net), fixing sections that had become outdated.

## Changes

- **Updated throughput numbers**: `~30 KB/s throughput over BLE` → `Up to ~59 KB/s throughput over BLE (Android 59.0, iOS 32.1, Python 30.3 KB/s)`
  - The old figure was effectively the Python-only number and had become stale; replaced with the platform-specific measurements shown on blerpc.net.
- **Added an Architecture section**: documents the three-layer protocol stack as described on blerpc.net.
  1. **Command Layer** — Wraps Protocol Buffer payloads with metadata
  2. **Encryption Layer** — Optional AES-128-GCM encryption following a 4-step key exchange
  3. **Container Layer** — Fragments data into MTU-sized containers for BLE transmission
  - Also notes that communication occurs through a single GATT characteristic using Write Without Response and Notify.

## Notes

SECURITY.md, CHANGELOG.md, and docs/firmware-guide.md were also reviewed and found consistent with blerpc.net. This PR is documentation-only.

items.title: Phase 2 (4/N): streaming observability metrics + benchmark --stream
items.body:
## Summary
- Adds dedicated Prometheus series for the streaming path instead of reusing the batcher's `vgate_ttft_seconds`/`vgate_tpot_seconds`: `vgate_stream_ttft_seconds`, `vgate_stream_tpot_seconds`, `vgate_stream_duration_seconds`, `vgate_stream_tokens_total`, `vgate_stream_requests_total{status="completed"|"error"|"cancelled"}`. Kept separate rather than adding a `mode` label to the existing series — the two paths measure fundamentally different things (vLLM engine-reported metrics vs. gateway-side wall clock against SSE chunk arrival), so mixing them would make neither queryable and would change the meaning of the existing series for every current caller/dashboard.
- TPOT is **token-weighted**: `decode_time / decode_tokens`, accumulated per delta from each delta's cumulative `num_tokens`, not a naive chunk-time average — a single SSE delta can carry more than one token (real vLLM chunks aren't always 1:1 with tokens).
- Fixes a real bug found while wiring up completed/error/cancelled status tracking: the old `finally: yield "data: [DONE]\n\n"` is illegal once a client disconnect delivers `GeneratorExit` to the generator — Python raises `RuntimeError: async generator ignored GeneratorExit` if you yield while handling it. Disconnects/cancellations (`GeneratorExit`, `asyncio.CancelledError`) are now caught explicitly, recorded as `status="cancelled"` (not counted as an inference error via `INFERENCE_ERRORS`), and skip that final yield.
- `benchmarks/bench_load.py --stream` now actually works (previously exited with "not implemented: see ROADMAP.md Phase 2"): sends `stream: true`, consumes SSE, and reports client-observed TTFT percentiles alongside the existing latency/throughput numbers. Its `tokens/sec` counts content-delta events (not exact token IDs, since V-Gate's SSE doesn't carry a final usage count yet) — documented as a relative-comparison caveat, not treated as exact.
- Updates `ROADMAP.md` (Phase 2 task 5 → done) and `README.md` (new metric names, `--stream` usage + caveat).

This closes ROADMAP.md Phase 2 task 5. Remaining Phase 2 work (SGLang async streaming backend, redefining `RequestBatcher` as admission/dedup/fan-out) is unchanged.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/test_streaming.py` (new `TestStreamingMetrics` class): successful stream records all 5 new metrics with correct deltas (count/sum, not absolute values, since Prometheus collectors are process-global); backend error mid-stream → `status="error"` + `INFERENCE_ERRORS` increment, `status="completed"` unchanged; simulated client disconnect (`gen.aclose()` mid-stream) → `status="cancelled"`, no exception, `INFERENCE_ERRORS`/`status="error"` unchanged; TPOT is token-weighted (multi-token deltas with real elapsed time via `asyncio.sleep`, not a monkeypatched clock — patching the global `time.monotonic` would also corrupt asyncio's and pytest's own timing, learned the hard way while writing this test).
- [x] `tests/test_bench_load.py`: markdown rendering with/without `stream` mode (TTFT rows present/absent).
- [x] **Verified both fixes are real regressions, not tautological tests**: temporarily reintroduced the chunk-averaged TPOT calculation and the unconditional `finally: yield`, confirmed the new tests fail against each (reproducing the exact `RuntimeError: async generator ignored GeneratorExit`), then restored the fix and confirmed green.
- [x] Full suites green: `VGATE_DRY_RUN=true pytest tests/` (159 passed) and `pytest vgate-client/tests/` (74 passed).
- [x] Live integration smoke test against a running dry-run server: ran `bench_load.py --stream`, confirmed `/metrics` shows correct sample counts (`vgate_stream_requests_total{status="completed"} 12`, etc.) after a 12-request run, and confirmed non-streaming mode is unaffected.

items.title: Offline-profiler benchmark scripts + measured Gate 1 numbers (memory ✓, throughput ✓, thermal documented)
items.body:
### Summary

Closes the M2 milestone of the ADTC 2026 Gate 1 track: this PR turns "we built an offline binder" into "we can **prove** its contest numbers". It adds a reproducible measurement toolkit (offline proof, profiler smoke, thread matrix, thermal soak), ships the measured results in `BENCHMARKS.md`, and freezes the empirically-best server configuration.

Every number in this PR was **measured on this build laptop** (Intel i7-8650U · 23.3 GB RAM · Ubuntu 22.04 · no GPU) — nothing invented. The application code is unchanged from Gate 1 (merged in #1).

### What changed (13 files: 5 modified, 8 new)

**New measurement scripts**
| Script | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `scripts/offline_check.sh` | Binder offline proof: credit / SOCA refuse / stock asserts + ledger flip-and-restore bind proof; re-runs asks inside `unshare -n` when available (airplane-mode proof) |
| `scripts/run_profiler_smoke.sh` | `adtc-profiler` participant mode → `benchmarks/raw/submission.json` + auto-generated `benchmarks/submission.summary.md`; optional `--full` accuracy pass |
| `scripts/thread_matrix.sh` | `llama-bench` thread bake-off (`-t 2,3,4,6,8`) with package-temp sampling after each run |
| `scripts/thermal_soak.sh` | 10-min sustained-generation soak (5 s sampling) → CSV + PASS/FAIL verdict; **enforces single-server measurement** (pre-flight port/process guard + in-loop contamination detection + FAIL on <100 % HTTP) |

**Config freeze**
- `scripts/start_llama_server.sh` — `THREADS=3` frozen from the thread matrix (`-t 3` = 17.94 tg_tps; `-t 8` collapsed TPS *and* hit 85 °C). Still overridable via env for experiments.

**Measured artifacts + docs**
- `BENCHMARKS.md` — all measured tables with run provenance; raw dumps stay gitignored under `benchmarks/raw/`
- `benchmarks/README.md`, `benchmarks/submission.summary.md`, `benchmarks/.gitignore`
- `REPORT.md`, `README.md`, `docs/CODE_WALKTHROUGH.md`, `docs/README.md` — updated to match measured reality

### Measured numbers (all from this laptop)

**Profiler smoke** (2026-08-04, `--skip-accuracy`)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Peak RSS | **1825.6 MB** (≪ 5.5 GB self-limit, ≪ 7 GB DQ) |
| Generation TPS | **14.73 tok/s** (reference ≈ 15) |
| TTFT | 9865.49 ms |
| Core temp peak | 100.0 °C — throttled ⚠️ |

**Thread matrix** (2026-08-05, `llama-bench -t 2,3,4,6,8`)

| threads | tg_tps | pp_tps | temp | note |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 2 | 14.96 | 45.79 | 76 °C | ok |
| **3** | **17.94** | 63.73 | 77 °C | **frozen default** |
| 4 | 16.57 | 62.52 | 76 °C | ok |
| 6 | 16.32 | 62.20 | 79 °C | ok |
| 8 | 7.53 | 59.74 | **85 °C** | hot — collapsed TPS |

**Thermal soak** (2026-08-06, `THREADS=3`, `ctx=2048`, single server, 10 min)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Samples / HTTP success | 75 / **100 %** |
| Temp mean | **78.1 °C** |
| Temp peak | **97.0 °C** (at +297 s) |
| ≥ 85 °C samples | 9/75 (12 %) |
| Verdict | **FAIL** on this 2018-era laptop |

### Thermal mitigation plan (honest status)

- Steady state is comfortable (mean 78 °C, no runaway) — the failure is **intermittent bursts**, same pattern as the 100 °C profiler smoke.
- **M2 is not closed on thermal** for this host. Ordered mitigations:
  1. Re-soak at `THREADS=2` (matrix measured 76 °C / 14.96 tg_tps there — ~17 % TPS cost for thermal headroom)
  2. `CTX=1024` + shorter `max_tokens` on the soak payload
  3. P_thermal is decided on the **official eval machine** (i5 12th-gen / Ryzen 5), which cools differently — record that run separately when available
- Memory ✓ and throughput ✓ buckets are measured and safe; thermal is the only open item and it is **documented, not hidden**.

### Validation

- `PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/ -q` → **19 passed** (Gate 1 suite unchanged)
- `ruff check app tests scripts` → clean
- `bash -n` on all 7 scripts → clean
- `bash scripts/offline_check.sh` → **PASS** (incl. ledger flip + restore)
- `bash scripts/smoke_narrate.sh` → **PASS** end-to-end: `source: binder+llm`, LLM restated exact binder figures (8410 XAF / 410 over / max 2 crates) — zero hallucination, `message` authoritative
- Negative test: soak pre-flight correctly **refuses** while another server runs (exit 1)

items.title: inference-server: fill sglang.md gaps, add missing unsloth.md sections (recreates #7)
items.body:
Recreates #7, which GitHub auto-closed during a history-rewrite attempt that was rolled back. Branch and commits are unchanged; the original review thread is still readable at #7.

The old PR object cannot be reopened — GitHub has latched it (`422 branch has no history in common with main`), and reopening was already exhausted via GraphQL, REST, and ref-update events. Head is still `d22a506`, identical to what #7 pointed at.

---

## Review status carried over from #7

- **This was approved-equivalent at the time it was closed.** No outstanding review objections; the close was purely the mechanical auto-close, not a review decision.
- **SGLang's official cookbook content was imported** in commit `d22a506`, on top of the original gap-filling commit `af14bbf`. Both commits are on this branch.
- The one follow-up the original called out is still a follow-up and still not in this PR: `inference-server/README.md:12` lists Unsloth as "Pending verified GGUF", which is stale.

---

## Original description (from #7, verbatim)

Addresses the team review of `inference-server/sglang.md` and `inference-server/unsloth.md`. Every command, flag and artifact name below was checked against a live source; anything that could not be verified is marked as pending on the page rather than dressed up as runnable.

## `sglang.md`

Review: structurally sound, but carries noticeably less information than the `ollama.md` template it was cloned from.

| Finding | Resolution |
|---|---|
| No endpoint URL | Added: SGLang serves an OpenAI-compatible endpoint on `:30000/v1`, with the base URL to point a harness at. Verified — `port` defaults to `30000` in `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`. |
| No reason given for why tool calling is unverified | Now says what is actually missing. SGLang *does* ship a Muse Glimmer tool-call parser (`--tool-call-parser muse` → `MuseGlimmerDetector`), but only on the upstream `muse-glimmer` branch (PR #34262) — not in `main` or any release — and no tool-calling round has been run for this cookbook. Verified by cloning the repo: `main` has no `muse` parser; the branch has `python/sglang/srt/function_call/muse_glimmer_detector.py` registered as `"muse"`. |
| No mechanism for setting stop tokens | Determined from source, and now documented. SGLang has no serve flag for it: `ModelConfig._get_hf_eos_token_id` **unions** `eos_token_id` from the checkpoint's `config.json` and its `generation_config.json`, so the checkpoint is where you set it. Because it is a union, nothing subtracts from that set afterwards — if either file lists the end-of-message token, SGLang stops on it and the fix is the checkpoint metadata. Per request, `stop_token_ids` can add ids but not remove them. |
| Serve command omits `--served-model-name` | Added. Verified that `served_model_name` defaults to `model_path` verbatim in `server_args.py`, so without it the model answers to `meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B` and every recipe in this cookbook — all of which send `"model": "muse-glimmer"` — fails to match. Also added `--reasoning-parser muse` / `--tool-call-parser muse` and the branch install step, matching SGLang's own verified command panel. |

Status banner updated to name the real blocker (support lives on an unreleased branch) instead of a bare "pending".

## `unsloth.md`

Review: the thinnest page in the directory — no Verify tool calling, no Next steps, no Stop tokens.

This page is partner-authored, and `README.md:17` explicitly sanctions partner pages keeping the vendor's own shape. So this change **preserves Unsloth's voice and its Fine-tuning section** and appends the missing sections, rather than flattening the page into our skeleton.

| Finding | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Missing Verify tool calling | Added, clearly marked not-yet-verified for Muse Glimmer, with the OpenAI-`tools` curl check against `:8888/v1/chat/completions`. Request shape and auth header taken from Unsloth's own Curl & HTTP integration doc. |
| Missing Stop tokens | Added, using the same wording pattern as `sglang.md` / `llama-cpp.md` — the folder README says this rule applies to every server here regardless of page shape. It states plainly that the Unsloth docs do not document a stop-token override and that Muse Glimmer's stop tokens have not been verified on this runtime, rather than guessing a mechanism. |
| Missing Next steps | Added, pointing back at the page's own Fine-tuning section, the agentic fundamentals, and the verified vLLM path. |
| Line ~22 circular "Manual installation" pointer | Removed. The section now goes straight to the terminal install it was already carrying. |
| Line ~86 triple-backtick inline code | Changed to single backticks. |
| Page ends on a CLI snippet naming an artifact that does not exist | **That GGUF now exists**: [`unsloth/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF), published today — confirmed via the HF API, and `UD-Q4_K_XL` is a real file (the old repo id's casing was wrong). Separately, `unsloth run` is **not** a documented command — Unsloth's CLI has `unsloth studio` and `unsloth start` — so the snippet is replaced with the documented `unsloth start <agent> --model <repo>:<QUANT> --context-length ...` form, and the section now closes with real context instead of trailing off. |

Status banner updated: the GGUF build is no longer pending; a verified tool-calling run still is.

## Notes

- No VRAM or throughput numbers added.
- `sglang.md` keeps the canonical section order; `unsloth.md` keeps its partner shape plus the three missing sections.
- All relative links in both pages resolve.
- **Follow-up, not in this PR:** `inference-server/README.md:12` still lists Unsloth as "Pending verified GGUF", which is now stale. Left untouched to avoid colliding with concurrent edits to that file.

items.title: docs: trust-claims evidence map and threat model
items.body:
## Summary

Adds the two audit deliverables that make FreshData's trust posture inspectable, both in the docs nav:

**`docs/trust-claims.md`** — every trust-relevant README/docs claim mapped to the test, benchmark, or measured boundary that proves it (superset of the machine-enforced `CLAIM_REGISTRY`). It also says the quiet parts out loud:
- the published CleanBench table's provenance is pinned to freshdata **1.0.0** — stale vs 1.1.1; regenerate or version-stamp the header
- the all-1.0000 precision/recall rows are regression floors on the public corruption suite (which the engine was developed against), not field expectations
- "modern laptop" throughput numbers are guidance backed by perf baselines, not promises
- the disclosed ECE 0.0384 > 0.03 gap stays disclosed

**`docs/threat-model.md`** — six trust boundaries with verified references: input parsing (zero eval/exec/pickle in `src/freshdata`, grep-verified), CSV formula injection stance per surface, copilot `model_context` guarantees per privacy mode (CLAIM_REGISTRY-enforced), provider-failure semantics (honest: a failing provider does not un-send data), regex-only PII detection as the #1 practitioner gotcha, and masking-token linkability — including that the **default HMAC salt is a public constant**, so low-cardinality tokens are guess-confirmable; a per-run salt would break documented reproducibility, recorded as a roadmap trade-off rather than silently changed.

## Verification

- Every factual statement verified against source or measured during the audit (privacy.py HMAC path, RSS benchmarks from #124, adversarial tests from #122, sanitizer tests from #123).
- `tests/test_cleanbench_public_release.py` (README claim audit) green — no registry wording touched.

items.body:
## What this is

The improvement round scoped from the TalkBass + r/BassGuitar + r/VSTi beta threads (no new sounds).

## Changes

- **Fuzz loudness match** — engaging FUZZ jumped each LO FX strip by **+11.2 / +16.1 / +11.4 dB** (57/421/tweeter), measured K-weighted with the new `tools/bor-bench` harness. The fuzz path now carries a calibrated trim; FX defaults and the Hysterical preset were raised to match so the shipped tone is identical, and old sessions are migrated on load (`stateVersion` gate) so existing mixes don't shift. Verified matched to within 0.03 dB.
- **Spectrum analyzer** — 8192-sample FFT with log-bin power averaging/interpolation (fixes the sub-500 Hz stair-steps reported on TalkBass), plus a second grey trace showing the raw DI under the cyan processed curve.
- **A/B** — audition the raw DI against the processed stack, 10 ms crossfade, deliberately not a saved parameter.
- **SYS panel** — live CPU (`AudioProcessLoadMeasurer`), latency, sample rate, block size, format, xruns.
- **Update notice** — checks the GitHub releases API at most once/day (cached, fail-silent), shows an amber UPDATE link when a newer tag exists.
- **App icon** — hex monogram tile replaces the macOS placeholder (source: `assets/bor-icon.svg`).
- **bor-bench** (`-DBOR_BUILD_TOOLS=ON`) — repeatable calibration + throughput numbers: worst case **~1.4 % of one Apple Silicon core** at 48 kHz/512; all-clean ~0.5 %.
- **README** — tech FAQ (signal flow, glue spec, oversampling/anti-aliasing, latency, CPU) in general terms + beginner glossary.

items.title: feat: bump default Postgres engine version to 18.4
items.body:
## Summary

Aligns this module's Postgres defaults with n8n's Postgres version policy (supported range is the latest two actively-maintained majors, currently 17 and 18, plus 16 as a time-limited compatibility tier; Aurora and other Postgres-compatible derivatives are out of official support scope). `db_engine_version` moves from `16.9` to `18.4`, and `examples/large`'s Aurora cluster moves from `16.4` to `18.4`. The Aurora example is kept rather than deleted, since its value is the I/O-Optimized throughput profile, but it now carries an explicit "not certified by n8n" caveat in both its README and `aurora.tf` so the support boundary is unambiguous at the point of use.

`18.4` was picked by querying the API the variable's own description points at, not by reading a release note: it is the newest available `postgres` minor in eu-west-1, us-east-1, and eu-central-1, is available for `aurora-postgresql` in all three, and is orderable with every instance class this repo defaults to (`db.t3.small`, `db.m6g.2xlarge`, `db.r6g.8xlarge`).

## Linked issue

Closes #84

## Stability impact

- [ ] **Patch-eligible**: additive only (new optional input, new output, new resource that doesn't disturb existing state, bug fix, docs).
- [x] **Minor-only**: changes existing defaults, renames or removes inputs, refactors resource addresses, or bumps provider version floors.

Changes the `db_engine_version` default. See the reviewer note below on what that does and does not do to existing state.

## Checklist

- [x] `terraform fmt -recursive` is clean.
- [x] `terraform validate` passes at the module root.
- [x] `terraform test -verbose` passes at the module root and on any example I touched.
- [x] `tflint --format compact` is clean at any directory I touched.
- [ ] If I added or renamed an input/output, I ran `terraform-docs markdown table --output-file README.md --output-mode inject .` and committed the refreshed README. **N/A**: no input or output was added or renamed. The generated table was still regenerated and committed, since `db_engine_version`'s default column changed.
- [ ] If I added a non-trivial new behavior, I added a plan-time assertion in the relevant `.tftest.hcl` file. **N/A**: no new behavior. Existing assertions in `tests/defaults.tftest.hcl` and `examples/large/tests/defaults.tftest.hcl` were updated to the new expected value.
- [x] If this is a minor-only change, I updated `CHANGELOG.md` under `[Unreleased]` with an upgrade note.
- [x] Conventional Commits style on the commit subject.

The full CI matrix was run locally against the pinned tool versions from `.github/workflows/terraform-tests.yml` (Terraform 1.9.8, tflint v0.53.0, terraform-docs v0.22.0), across all seven matrix targets: `fmt`, `docs`, `validate`, `tflint` all clean, `terraform test` 187/187 passing. Checkov is byte-identical to the pre-change baseline (171 passed / 28 failed / 7 skipped, same per-check inventory), verified by scanning a `git archive` of the base commit and diffing.

## Notes for the reviewer

**This changes a default, not existing infrastructure.** `aws_db_instance.n8n` carries `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [engine_version] }` (`database.tf:282`), as do the Aurora cluster and both of its instances. Terraform ignores the difference between config and prior state for that attribute, so a changed default produces no plan diff on already-provisioned infrastructure. The new default applies only to instances created after this change. Existing instances stay on whatever is in state until upgraded deliberately out-of-band (`aws rds modify-db-instance --engine-version ... --apply-immediately`, or a console-driven major-version upgrade), after which `ignore_changes` lets Terraform adopt the new value on refresh instead of fighting it. The CHANGELOG entry spells this out so the bump is not read as either an automatic upgrade or a no-op.

**Aurora: keep-with-caveat over delete.** #84 left this open. Deleting the example would throw away the I/O-Optimized sizing work, which is the only reference in this repo for the ~50-60M executions/day tier and is orthogonal to the engine version. Documenting the support boundary keeps that value while making the policy position explicit at the two places a user would actually encounter it.

**One test assertion was reworded, not just renumbered.** `examples/large/tests/defaults.tftest.hcl` previously read "pinned to 16.4 (validated against PgBouncer + n8n TypeORM)". Only the storage-throughput numbers were ever benchmarked, not 18.4 specifically against TypeORM, so the new message claims only what is true: the pin tracks the newest supported major. The stale `16.13` in the root suite's `custom_database_sizing` run is intentional and untouched, since that run tests variable propagation rather than the default.

**Known precondition not met.** #84 notes that CI should ideally exercise the full supported Postgres range before this default moves (tracked separately in DEVP-676). This PR does not add that coverage.

| | Module-managed RDS (`db_engine_version` default) | Aurora (`examples/large`) |
|---|---|---|
| Live engine version | `18.4`, `available` | `18.4`, `available` (writer + reader) |
| Smoke test (`tests/scripts/smoke-test.sh`) | 31/31 pass | 31/31 pass |
| Sustained webhook-triggered load | 340/340 succeeded (30 min) | 57/57 succeeded (5 min) |
| DB-layer errors observed | 0 | 0 |

Both runs used the module's own defaults (no overrides), the Aurora run at the example's full production sizing (`db.r6g.8xlarge` x2, 10-50x `m7i.4xlarge` nodes). Neither showed connection resets, pool exhaustion, or auth failures at any point.

items.title: docs(readme): rigorously honest benchmarks + claim→proof mapping
items.body:
## What

Makes the Holdfast README recruiter/Stripe-grade honest: every quantitative claim now maps to a runnable command, benchmark numbers reflect a freshly measured local run, and the one internally-inconsistent comparison is called out explicitly.

## Why

The README's benchmark numbers had drifted ~15% high vs current hardware, the proof block claimed a stale "9 passed" (the suite is 14 tests), and two "single hot row" throughput numbers (strategy ~4,200 vs sharded 1-shard ~14,000) looked contradictory because they actually time **different operations** — never stated. A careful reviewer would catch all three.

## Changes (all docs-only)

- **Re-measured both benchmarks** against real local Postgres 16 and updated to a representative run:
  - Strategy (`npm run bench 2000 3`, full `reserve()` path): atomic ~3,600 / pessimistic ~3,650 / optimistic ~2,800 res/s @ 2.01 avg CAS attempts.
  - Sharded (`npm run bench:sharded 2000 3`, bare `reserveSharded` UPDATE): 1→~13.7k, 4→~28k, 16→~46k, 64→~46k. Plateau is ~3.3× (was claimed 3.5×).
- **Resolved the apparent contradiction**: added a callout that the sharded table times the bare autocommit `UPDATE` while the strategy table times the full transaction (idempotency + order insert) — not comparable; the claim is the relative curve, not absolute res/s.
- **Framed every benchmark** as a single-machine local result with the exact rerun command; the reproducible takeaway is the ordering/shape, not the exact figures.
- **Fixed the proof block**: "9 passed" → the real suite is **14 tests across 6 files**, each line mapped to its test file.
- Softened "the hardest correctness problem" → "a core correctness problem" (kept test-backed "never oversells").

## Gate

Docs-only change; verified the underlying claims still hold on real Postgres 16:
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm test` — **14/14 passing** across 6 files
- `npm run bench 2000 3` and `npm run bench:sharded 2000 3` — ran; README numbers reflect these runs.

## Claim → proof mapping

| README claim | Backed by |
|---|---|
| never oversells (500 buyers @ 50, ×3 strategies) | `test/concurrency.test.ts` |
| idempotent: same key ×100 → ONE reservation | `test/idempotency.test.ts` |
| 100 opposite-order baskets, 0 deadlocks | `test/basket.test.ts` |
| aggregate no-oversell across shards | `test/sharded.test.ts` |
| fails closed under ~100 killed transactions | `test/chaos.test.ts` (STOCK=50, BUYERS=400; observed winners=50, terminated=115) |
| expired holds return stock | `test/lifecycle.test.ts` |
| strategy throughput / latency / CAS table | `npm run bench` → `src/bench.ts` |
| sharded relative curve (~3.3× plateau) | `npm run bench:sharded` → `src/sharded-bench.ts` |

Phase 5.1 wants throughput/latency numbers trending **in CI** — but there was no CI at all. This adds both: a GitHub Actions workflow and two headless throughput benchmarks.

GUI-dependent measurements (typometer-style **added input latency**, scrollback memory) stay documented manual/local checks — a headless CI runner has no display to measure frame latency reliably. Noted in ROADMAP Phase 5.1.

items.title: Write per-row value data by default, add -no-random-data to opt out
items.body:
## Problem

By default `GenerateData` returns an all-zero blob for the value column when `-validate-data` is off (the default). With a fixed `-clustering-row-size`, **every row's `v` value is byte-identical**.

When an MV nemesis (`KillMVBuildingCoordinator`, `AddRemoveMvNemesis`) creates a materialized view keyed on `v`, all view rows hash to a single token → one partition → one shard per replica. That shard drowns under view-build backpressure: `view_update_sl:default` semaphore saturation and commitlog segments that never free. Identical blobs also make compression tests unrealistically compressible.

Refs: QATOOLS-276 (root cause — asks for exactly this, a random blob instead of a zero-initialized one, and notes the compression side effect), SCYLLADB-2876 (an occurrence of the resulting overload).

## Fix

Per-row value data is now the **default**, with `-no-random-data` to opt out. The non-validate write path fills the value blob via the existing `fillPayload(pk, ck)` helper — unlocked xorshift, high-entropy, **distinct per `(pk, ck)`**, deterministic:

- Distinct-per-key spreads the view token across the cluster, so a view keyed on `v` distributes normally.
- Deterministic → reproducible benchmarks; cheaper than a CSPRNG.
- Threaded through `ExecutionConfig.RandomData` (`!noRandomData`), consumed by the single, batched and mixed write paths.
- `-no-random-data` restores the previous byte-for-byte all-zero payload.
- No effect when `-validate-data` is set — that path already writes distinct per-row data and returns before consulting the flag.

### Short values

`fillPayload` writes a 64-bit xorshift word per 8 bytes. A non-zero state never produces a zero word, so any value of 8+ bytes is inherently non-zero — but a shorter value truncates the word and *can* come out all zeros. `ensureNonZero` closes that hole, so **non-zeroness holds for every accepted size**.

**Cardinality cannot be guaranteed for short values and is not claimed**: a 1-byte value has at most 256 distinct values regardless of row count, so an MV keyed on it still ends up with few partitions. Both the flag help and the README say so and recommend `-clustering-row-size` ≥ 8 when view cardinality matters.

## Notes

- **Behavior change**: runs that don't pass `-no-random-data` now write incompressible payloads, so throughput numbers on compressed tables are no longer comparable with historical baselines. Pass `-no-random-data` to reproduce old numbers.
- SCT needs no change to benefit — the default now fixes the affected write commands.
- The categorical fix arguably still belongs in SCT: `create_materialized_view_for_random_column` picking a low-cardinality column as a view partition key is an anti-pattern regardless of the payload.

## Testing

- `TestGenerateDataRandomData` — non-zero, deterministic per key, distinct across pk and ck; legacy path still all-zero.
- `TestGenerateDataRandomDataShortSizes` — sizes 1–7 across 512 pk × 4 ck, all non-zero (cardinality deliberately not asserted).
- `TestDefaultExecutionConfigRandomData` — 4-way table over `(-no-random-data, -validate-data)` pinning the flag to `ExecutionConfig.RandomData`.
- `TestIntegrationRandomData` — dedicated table per case; runs `DoWrites` / `DoBatchedWrites` / `DoMixed` × on/off through the real config plumbing and reads the persisted `v` column back from ScyllaDB, asserting non-zero and >1 distinct value when enabled, and exactly one all-zero value when disabled. **Verified green against a real 2025.2 container** (all 6 subtests pass).
- `BenchmarkGenerateDataWithValidation/with_random_data` added alongside the existing cases.
- Full package suite, `go vet` and `golangci-lint` all clean.

Also records the retry semantics in ROADMAP — which failures are safe to retry on another worker is a design decision, not an implementation detail — and notes that streaming through a worker returns 501.

Its checklist and Next Steps table describe a Ray/RunPod plan that was never taken. Editing them in place would erase the record of the direction change, so they are marked as a historical snapshot with an added outcome column showing what actually shipped instead.

## Summary

Adds **IOR** (https://github.com/hpc/ior), the standard parallel-filesystem benchmark, as a new HPC synthetic benchmark for storage/disk I/O — primarily **Amazon FSx for Lustre**. Follows the existing OSU/HPL utility conventions.

## What's included (`Utils/IOR/`)

  - directory striping across all OSTs (`lfs setstripe -c -1`)

items.title: Size ingest defaults to the annotation budget: 10 candidates/query, 1K retrieval depth
items.body:
> ♻️ Recreated from #17 (closed, branch unchanged) to trigger a CodeRabbit review.

Closes #12.

## The problem

`candidates_per_query` defaulted to **5,000**, and every kept candidate needs `required_annotations` (2) labels. The math:

| | queries | pairs @5,000/query | annotations needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| squad (smallest split) | ~87k | ~435M | ~870M |
| paq | 65M | 3.25×10¹¹ | 6.5×10¹¹ |

At the README's own throughput numbers (RTX 4090 ≈ 57.6k pairs overnight), 100 always-on 4090s need **~150 days for squad's candidates alone**. The landing-page goal of 1B labeled pairs is the *total* budget; the old default spent ~40% of it on one split's candidate tail. Worse, batches are claimed oldest-first, so contributors would grind through 5,000 negatives for the earliest queries before anything else — and retrieval ranks in the thousands aren't hard negatives at all, they're easy negatives that in-batch sampling already handles for free.

## The change

- `candidates_per_query`: **5,000 → 10** (ANCE/CDE-style hard-negative mining uses single-digit-to-low-double-digit counts per query)
- `bm25_top_k` / `dense_top_k`: **10,000 → 1,000** (ample fusion depth when only the top 10 survive; ~10× faster per-query retrieval)
- CLI flags unchanged in shape — any depth remains available for experiments
- `ingest-implementation.md` pipeline sketch, CLI reference, and timing estimates updated
- Regression test guards the budget (`candidates_per_query ≤ 50`, retrieval depth ≤ 2,000) so the default can't silently creep back up

New default budget: squad → ~870k pairs → ~1.74M annotations, i.e. **a weekend for a small fleet instead of a quarter**, with coverage growth coming from iterative re-mining with the improved model (already the manifesto's plan) rather than deeper static lists.

## Cleanup for already-ingested data (not in this PR)

If squad was already ingested at the old depth: `DELETE FROM pairs WHERE source_rank > 10 AND status = 'unlabeled'` reclaims the queue; deterministic uuid5 IDs make any re-ingest idempotent. The website pipeline diagram's "top-5,000 candidates per query" text is updated separately in embedkombinat.github.io#2.

## Verification

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy kombinat/` clean; ingest test suite 49 passed (1 new test).

items.body:
## Commit Summary (Conventional Commits) - Title (required, present tense): ```text docs(adr): add ADR 0002 native hashing decision ``` - Type: - [ ] feat (minor) - [ ] fix / perf (patch) - [x] docs - [ ] refactor - [ ] test - [ ] chore / ci / style - Breaking change: - [ ] `!` in title or `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer included ## What’s Changing Adds ADR 0002 evaluating a Rust native batch hasher versus pure Python imagehash. Recommendation: adopt Python imagehash now; defer Rust until hash compute (not I/O) is proven to dominate real library scans. ## Checklist - [x] Title follows Conventional Commits - [ ] Tests added/updated - [x] Docs updated if user-facing - [x] Local CI passed (`make lint && make test`) ## Closes - Closes #44 ## Details Includes microbenchmark methodology, throughput numbers, and re-evaluation triggers. Updates the ADR index.
  

Greptile Summary

 This PR adds ADR 0002 documenting the decision to adopt the pure-Python `imagehash` library over a Rust native extension for perceptual hashing, backed by microbenchmark data and explicit re-evaluation triggers. It also adds the new ADR to the index and widens the markdownlint ignore list to cover agent-generated directories. - **ADR 0002** (`docs/adr/0002-native-hashing.md`): documents single-threaded throughput, threading-scaling data, and rationale for deferring a Rust/PyO3 extension; includes a helpful explanatory note resolving the previously flagged baseline discrepancy between the two benchmark tables. - **README index** (`docs/adr/README.md`): adds the ADR 0002 row with correct date and status. - **Linter config** (`.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc`): excludes `.agent-prompts/**` and `.agent-skills/**` from markdownlint scans.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge after fixing the license label — the rest of the ADR is well-reasoned and accurate. The ADR incorrectly states that `imagehash` is MIT-licensed when it is BSD-2-Clause. Because ADRs are treated as authoritative records and may inform compliance decisions downstream, a wrong license declaration is a real factual error rather than a stylistic nit. docs/adr/0002-native-hashing.md — specifically the license attribution in the Consequences section.

items.title: Add pluggable CDC ingest benchmark framework (test/cdcbench)
items.body:
### Describe the changes in this pull request

The live-migration import streaming path (`streamChangesFromSegment` and everything under it: NDJSON decode, name-registry lookups, Debezium value conversion, the conflict-detection cache, event channels, batching) had no repeatable way to measure ingest throughput or conflict-detection behavior. This PR adds a benchmark framework that replays **real Debezium-generated change events** through the **unmodified production import code**, with exactly one mock: `TargetDB.ExecuteBatch` succeeds without a database.

Design:
- **Workloads are pluggable**: a workload = 3 SQL files (schema/seed/DML) + a ~10-line `Register()` call in `test/cdcbench`. Four founding workloads at 20k events each span the behavior space: `inserts-no-uk` (control), `updates-uk-no-conflict`, `mixed-uk-no-conflict` (60/30/10 op mix), `updates-uk-conflict-pairs` (10k engineered unique-key conflicts).
- **Artifacts are real and cached**: events are generated once by an actual `yb-voyager export data` (snapshot-and-changes) run against a testcontainers PostgreSQL source (`wal_level=logical`), then cached keyed by a content hash of the workload definition. Editing a workload's SQL auto-invalidates only its artifact; cached artifacts replay with no Docker or voyager-binary dependency.
- **Clean layering**: `test/cdcbench` has zero knowledge of the `cmd` package. The three pieces needing cmd internals are injected as closures (`Bootstrap`, `StreamAll`, `CacheDepth`) by a thin shim `cmd/cdc_ingest_bench_test.go` behind the `cdc_benchmark` build tag. **No production code changes.**
- **Measured, not assumed**: per run the framework reports events/s, batches, and conflict-cache depth (100ms sampler), and *asserts* the exact processed-event count plus the workload's conflict expectation (zero vs non-zero, counted via a logrus hook on the cache's conflict logs). Output is both benchstat-compatible `Benchmark` lines and a human summary table.

Motivation: recent conflict-detection work needed before/after throughput numbers; this framework reproduces that methodology as a first-class, reusable tool. Baseline on current main (Apple M1 Pro): `inserts-no-uk` ~129k events/s vs `updates-uk-no-conflict` ~1.1k events/s (conflict-cache scans; depth ~1.4k) — the ~100× gap this framework exists to track.

### Describe if there are any user-facing changes

No user-facing changes. No CLI, configuration, installation, or report changes. The framework is a test-support library plus a build-tag-gated test file; released binaries are unaffected (`go build ./...` compiles identically).

### How was this pull request tested?

- `go vet` and `staticcheck` clean on `test/cdcbench/` and on `cmd/` with `-tags cdc_benchmark`; `go build ./...` unaffected.
- End-to-end on Apple M1 Pro (Docker + installed yb-voyager with debezium-server): artifact generation validated for all four workloads (~1 min each, one-time), then
  `go test -tags cdc_benchmark -run '^$' -bench CDCIngest -benchtime 1x ./cmd/`
  runs the full suite from cache in ~31s. All per-run assertions pass: exact event counts (20,000 per workload) and conflict expectations (0 conflicts for the three no-conflict workloads; ~14k detections for `updates-uk-conflict-pairs`).
- Graceful skip verified: without a `yb-voyager` binary on PATH (and no cached artifact), the benchmark skips with instructions rather than failing.
- Not wired into CI (needs Docker + installed voyager/Debezium for generation); documented as a local tier in CLAUDE.md and `test/cdcbench/README.md`.

### Does your PR have changes in callhome/yugabyted payloads? If so, is the payload version incremented?

No.

### Does your PR have changes to on-disk structures that can cause upgrade issues?

No. The framework only reads/writes its own generated benchmark artifacts (gitignored `test/cdcbench/artifacts/`); it never touches user migration state. Within its own artifacts it writes both historical variants of the unique-key metaDB key so artifacts replay identically across voyager versions — a benchmark-local concern, not an on-disk format change.

items.title: Simulator and rollout performance: +10% training throughput, behaviour identical
items.body:
Three behaviour-preserving optimisations to `sim/` and `rl/`. **+10% end-to-end training throughput** on a 5600X + RTX 3080, with `simcheck` and `veccheck` digests byte-identical to `master`.

Happy to drop or split any of it.

## Verification

Everything is gated on your own tools, not mine:

```
simcheck configs/sword.toml 256 2000
  master: all=f0c11ca862577356 obs=72a22fcc29b45347 rew=bae59f7e7b5650c6   755 episodes
  this:   all=f0c11ca862577356 obs=72a22fcc29b45347 rew=bae59f7e7b5650c6   755 episodes

veccheck configs/sword.toml 256 100
  1d87408f2753cfae, PASS across 1/3/8/16 workers, fused and unfused
```

Every commit was checked against those digests individually, not just the final state.

## Results

| | master | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| training throughput (4608 envs, autotuned) | 1,787,360 sps | **1,966,094 sps (+10.0%)** |
| `clientPlayerTick` in isolation, 1 core | 3.39 M turns/s | **8.13 M turns/s (+140%)** |
| `sizeof(Sim)` | 19.8 KiB/env | **16.8 KiB/env** |

Three paired runs of 180 s each, both orders, to rule out thermal bias: +10.5%, +6.6%, +10.7%. `master` is tight across runs (0.9% spread); the +6.6% is the outlier.

## What's in it

**`sim: collision and pose fast paths for the arena`**

The two that matter are both "don't do work that is provably absent", in the same spirit as your existing `deepInsideDisc` fast path:

- *Cross-tick pose fit proof.* `Entity.move` clips movement so the resulting AABB intersects nothing — which is exactly what `canFit` asks, on a box `canFit` then shrinks by `1e-7`. So after `moveEntity` the current pose is proven, and since poses differ only in height, a proven pose implies any shorter one. Removes **98.6%** of pose queries.
- *Flat-floor collapse.* Inside the disc `Arena::solid` is true only at `y=-1`. For a box at `minY >= 0` the strict `cubeOverlapPerp(minY,maxY,-1,0)` is false, so X and Z can never clip and auto-step can never fire — the gather, the `BoxList` and the three-pass scan collapse to one comparison. Fires on **99.98%** of ticks in a real duel.

Plus tighter collision cell bounds (the loops scanned 9–16 cells where at most 4 can match), a memoised movement-input vector (18 reachable outcomes, recomputed every tick with 3 sqrts and 4 divides), and three smaller items.

**`sim/net: shrink Pkt, hand drained packets over by reference`**

`Pkt` is written three times per delivery — zero-init, copy into the ring, copy back out on drain — at ~7 packets/env-tick. `perf` attributed ~19% of `Sim::step` to those stores. Bitfields + right-sized ints take it 112 → 88 B; `drain` now retires the slot after the handler returns so the packet passes by reference.

**`rl: hoist the ego basis, fold the reward shaping scale`**

`egoFrame` recomputed `sin`/`cos` of the same yaw six times per agent-tick. `CombinedReward::step` recomputed `shaped ? weight * scale_ : weight` for all 14 parts every tick, for a value that only changes in `onUpdate`.

## Two findings that aren't code

**1. Collect is the bottleneck, not the GPU.** `c220‖u133+92ms` — the learner stalls ~92 ms per update waiting on the collector, so the GPU sits around 50%. I swept the knobs and your autotuner already picks the optimum: workers 8/10/12 gave flat/−3.7%/−5.3%, chunk 4/20/32 gave −1.5%/−4.5%/−6.5%, torch_threads 4/6 gave −2.4%/−2.0%. The loop is memory-bandwidth bound, so more threads add contention. The only lever is making collect cheaper.

**2. `num_envs` is bounded by RAM, never by cache** (`autotune.cpp:207-217`) — but you probably shouldn't "fix" that. Stepping every env once per tick means the working set between two ticks of the same env is `numEnvs × perEnvBytes`, and in isolation the cliff is sharp (2048 envs 5.95 M env-ticks/s → 4096 envs 3.99 M → 8192 envs 3.06 M). I implemented an LLC clamp and it made training **slower**: the narrower policy-forward batch costs more on the GPU than the locality gains. 1280 envs measured worse than 4608 for both builds. Recording it because the isolated measurement is very convincing and very wrong.

## Not attempted

Folding `Pkt`'s mutually exclusive field groups into a union would reach ~56 B and is the largest remaining single win (~5%), but it needs either reads of inactive union members or rewriting ~50 call sites — and no digest can catch a field placed in the wrong group. Didn't feel like a good trade in someone else's codebase.

## Notes

Measured with a standalone benchmark harness I kept out of this PR to avoid noise. Happy to send it separately if useful — it builds `sim/` without LibTorch and reports env-ticks/s *and* agent-steps/s from the same run, which makes throughput numbers comparable across machines and configs (one `Sim::step` is 4 player ticks: two `clientPlayerTick` plus two `serverPlayerAiStep`).

Unrelated build note: on CPU LibTorch the `__has_include(<c10/cuda/CUDAStream.h>)` guards in `autotune.cpp` and `train.cpp` pass because the headers ship with it, but `libtorch_cuda` doesn't — so `train` fails to link on undefined `at::cuda::CUDAGraph`. `veccheck`/`simcheck` build fine. A cu-flavoured LibTorch fixes it; might be worth a line in the README.

items.title: Honor storage.compression on upgraded databases, and let a deployment select the codec
items.body:
`rocksdb-js` 2.6.1 (#2036) brought the codecs in and made lz4 the effective default. This fixes the case that default silently misses, and adds a way to choose a different codec.

## The bug: upgraded databases ignore `storage.compression`

`storage.compression` defaults to **`true`** (`config/defaultConfig.yaml`), so essentially every existing table's metadata records "compression enabled". `toRocksCompression` mapped that to *unset*, on the documented assumption that unset means "use the build default (lz4)".

It doesn't — not for a column family that already exists. RocksDB persists the codec per family, and a reopen that requests nothing **inherits what the family already has**; the build default applies only when the family is being created. Measured across separate processes:

```
5.1 instance, compression 'none'          -> 34.2M SST
5.2 instance, no option passed
    open -> engine reports {"algorithm":"none"}    <-- inherited, not lz4
                                          -> 68.4M SST   (new writes uncompressed too)
full compact()                            -> 68.4M SST   (unchanged)

control: same records, lz4 from scratch   ->  7.1M SST
```

So a brand-new 5.2 database gets lz4 while every database upgraded from 5.1 keeps writing uncompressed indefinitely — both having asked for exactly the same thing. New databases only worked by accident, because unset on a *non-existent* family does fall through to the build default.

An enabled setting now resolves to an explicit codec. On the real metadata path (`{ startingOffset, threshold }`, what `getDefaultCompression()` returns when `storage.compression` is true):

```
old:      opened 'none' -> reports none -> 31.6M SST
upgraded: opened 'lz4'  -> reports lz4  -> 33.9M SST   (the next 60k records cost 2.3M, not 31.6M)
```

**Existing data is deliberately left alone.** An explicit codec governs newly written files only, and `db.compact()` won't convert the rest: rocksdb-js calls `CompactRange` with default `CompactRangeOptions`, whose `bottommost_level_compaction` is `kIfHaveCompactionFilter`, and Harper installs no compaction filter — the bottommost level, holding the bulk of the data, is skipped. Converting in place needs a forced bottommost compaction, which is expensive enough to deserve an explicit operator decision rather than happening during an upgrade.

## Choosing a codec

`HARPER_STORAGE_ROCKS_COMPRESSION` selects the codec for every column family the process opens, validated against the build's `supportedCompression` so an unavailable name fails with a named error instead of a partial startup failure at the first open.

It's an env var and not a config key, and resolved once at module load, because RocksDB rejects reopening a family under a disagreeing codec and Harper's worker threads share one process-wide family registry — so every thread must agree. A config value doesn't achieve that; the main thread loads the storage layer during install, before the value is readable, while workers load it after:

```
pid=3591555 thread=0 resolved=undefined   <-- main thread, loads during install
pid=3591555 thread=1 resolved=zstd
pid=3591555 thread=2 resolved=zstd
```

`__dbis__` is then opened at the build default and reopened as the configured codec, and Harper dies with `The system database failed to load`. Reproduced on a fresh install with the value in config only; it fails on every boot. Making it a config key needs the value resolvable before the first family opens — a boot-ordering change, deliberately not in this PR, and the constraint is recorded in `DESIGN.md` so it doesn't get "improved" into one.

`copyDb`'s `openRocksDb` now resolves the codec the same way. `DESIGN.md` already called `openRocksDatabase` the single chokepoint and migration sat outside it — it creates the families the runtime later reopens.

## Benchmark

`benchmarks/compression/` compares codecs on identical data and workload, one instance per codec. On 1M document-shaped records:

| codec | data files | vs none |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none | 846 MB | 100% |
| snappy | 434 MB | 51% |
| lz4 | 454 MB | 54% |
| zstd | 351 MB | 41% |

Point reads get *faster* with compression — compressed blocks hold more records per block-cache slot and that outweighs decompression (lz4 nearly doubles point-read throughput at the storage layer). Sequential scans pay decompression with no cache-density offset and get slower.

Two traps the harness guards, both of which produce confidently wrong numbers: `@harperfast/integration-testing` installs under `os.tmpdir()`, which is tmpfs on most Linux hosts (every "on-disk" byte becomes a memory measurement); and Harper answers 503 once commits back up past `storage.maxTransactionQueueTime` — one run shed ~99% of its writes and still produced a throughput figure and a 67 MB "compressed" size, which reads as a spectacular win. Runs over an error-rate threshold are marked `INVALID`.

## Open concerns for the reviewer

- **The `toRocksCompression` change alters behavior for every existing table**, which is the point, but it's the line to scrutinize. `false`/`''` still map to `'none'`; an explicit `{ algorithm }` still passes through untouched; only "enabled, unspecified" changes meaning.
- **Benchmark sizes are as the workload left them, not a compacted steady state** — for the reason above, nothing outside the process can force a compaction. Codec-to-codec comparison is sound (identical workload each); the absolute ratio against logical bytes is inflated by update garbage. A storage-layer run using a real `db.compact()` agrees within 3 points.
- **Throughput numbers are single-sample, fixed codec order.** REST-layer variance swamps the codec differences; the size columns are the reliable output. Noted in the README.
- **Reads never touched a device** — the dataset fits in page cache. This measures decompression CPU and block-cache density, not I/O savings; an I/O-bound instance should look better.
- `openRocksDb` is a behavior change on the migration path — right side of the stated invariant, but worth a second pair of eyes.

Follow-up worth doing: expose forced bottommost compaction in rocksdb-js so an existing database can be converted on an explicit operator decision.

Cross-model review (Codex + Gemini + Grok + Harper-domain) ran pre-push; its findings on a no-op compaction step, a `scanBytesRead` race, the `copyDb` bypass, missing validation, committed result JSONs and missing docs are all addressed.

items.title: Add prompt-lookup (n-gram) speculative decoding
items.body:
## Summary
- Adds prompt-lookup decoding: draft continuation tokens by matching the current generation suffix against n-grams already present in the request context, then verify the draft in **one** batched forward pass. It needs **no extra model assets** (unlike draft-model speculative decode) and **no architecture support** (unlike native MTP), so it is the only acceleration mode available for an arbitrary locally imported model with nothing extra to download. The win comes from input-grounded workloads: RAG answers quoting retrieved passages, code edits echoing surrounding code, summarization, and agent turns repeating tool schemas.
- **`worker/runtime/prompt_lookup.py`** — the decoder, deliberately MLX-free and driven by an injected `step_fn`, so the propose → verify → accept loop is exercised end to end with deterministic fakes rather than mocked at the seams.
- **`worker/runtime/prompt_lookup_mlx.py`** — the real KV-cache-backed verify step. It reconciles cache position from the authoritative context on every call instead of tracking accept/reject bookkeeping, which makes it correct for *any* acceptance pattern (including a fully rejected draft) without the step needing to know what the previous cycle accepted. A cache that cannot trim to an arbitrary boundary (rotating / some quantized layouts) is rebuilt and re-prefilled rather than reused misaligned.
- Opt-in through `AccelerationPolicy.ext`, so **no protocol change**; the control plane forwards those keys to the worker with request `ext` winning over the session policy.

### Correctness: greedy identity
Verification accepts the longest draft prefix matching the target model's own greedy predictions, then emits one bonus token from the same forward. Every emitted token is therefore a prediction the model made, so the sequence is **identical to plain greedy decoding** — only the forward count differs. Proposing zero tokens degenerates to exactly the baseline path, which is why the hysteresis fallback costs nothing.

Consequently this mode is **greedy-only**: sampled requests (`temperature > 0` and `top_k != 1`) and structured-output requests stay on the standard path rather than silently changing their output distribution to gain throughput. Preserving a sampled distribution needs the stochastic accept / residual-sampling rule, which is out of scope here and noted as future work.

### Two design points worth calling out
- **Earliest-occurrence indexing.** The n-gram index maps each n-gram to its *earliest* end position. That biases drafts toward the grounded prompt/document rather than the model's own recent output, and it makes "the only occurrence is the suffix I am matching right now" detectable (stored position equals current context end) — precisely the case where no draft exists.
- **Hysteresis counts only drafted cycles.** Cycles that proposed nothing are not observations: with no draft there is no wasted verify width to protect against, so they must not dilute the accept-rate window or push it toward a pointless pause. Building the test for this surfaced the distinction — an early version of the adversarial test passed for the wrong reason (nothing was ever proposed, so nothing needed protecting).

Closes #2606. Related: #2602 (MTP generalization), #350 (acceleration profiles — this is a zero-asset profile option).

## Plan or Spec
- Issue #2606 defines the scope. Runbook added at `docs/runbooks/prompt-lookup-decoding.md` and indexed in `docs/README.md`.

## Commands Run
```text
uv run --project services/mlx-worker-python --extra mlx pytest \
  services/mlx-worker-python/tests/test_prompt_lookup.py \
  services/mlx-worker-python/tests/test_prompt_lookup_runtime.py -q
→ 49 passed

uv run ... pytest test_prompt_lookup.py test_prompt_lookup_runtime.py \
  test_mlx_backend.py test_generate_stream.py test_runtime_edges.py -q
→ 199 passed, 4 skipped

uv run ... pytest services/mlx-worker-python/tests -q   (full suite)
```

items.title: chore: EntityId Migration + Finalized Test Migration

## Description

This PR updates DxMessaging for Unity's `EntityId` migration and completes the no-yield PlayMode test migration.

What changed:
- Switched Unity object identity reads to a single version-gated source, `InstanceId.StableId`, to keep compatibility with Unity 6.4+ deprecations and Unity 6.5+ compile behavior while preserving the same 32-bit dispatch key.
- Updated runtime/editor call sites that previously read `GetInstanceID()` directly to use the shared stable-id source.
- Added `InstanceIdSourceTests` to lock migration behavior and guard against new direct `GetInstanceID()` usage outside the gated source.
- Converted remaining no-yield PlayMode `[UnityTest]` methods to plain `[Test]` and tightened the contract test so the migration allowlist is now empty.
- Updated user docs (`README`, compatibility, comparisons, and test-performance runbook) and internal AI testing guidance to reflect the completed migration and current benchmark framing.

User-facing impact:
- No public API changes.
- Package remains compatible across supported Unity versions, including Unity 6.5+ where `GetInstanceID()` is removed.
- PlayMode test maintenance and runtime test performance improve by removing unnecessary coroutine wrappers.

Fixes #208

items.title: chore(bench): #189 dotnet-counters capture identifies Npgsql pool exhaustion
items.body:
## Summary

Lands the dotnet-counters capture from the #189 investigation. **Does NOT close #189** — the investigation found the root cause but the fix is separate work tracked on the issue thread.

## Top finding

`dotnet-counters` against the vs SUT under sustained 5k and 8k target NBomber load shows **Npgsql connection pool exhaustion** is the dominant load-coupled bottleneck:

- `db.client.connection.count[used]` **pegs at the 500-connection pool ceiling** on both runs
- `db.client.connection.npgsql.pending_requests` shows **mean 2,000-4,000 requests in the wait queue**
- Postgres query duration p99 stays under 1s — Postgres itself is fine
- ThreadPool, GC pause, allocation rate, lock contention all show normal counter values — ruled out

The per-request latency premium that scales with offered load lives in waiting for a connection.

## Methodology caveats

The capture has known limitations (documented in the findings doc):
1. SUT ran JIT, not AOT (`vswhere.exe` toolchain miss on Windows for the AOT publish step)
2. Both 5k and 8k runs were below the 2026-06-05 reference baseline due to JIT cold-start + EventPipe counter overhead on a 4-core slice — measured "mid-collapse vs deeper-collapse" rather than "healthy vs collapsing"
3. The counter-shape evidence (pool used pegged in both runs) is still solid; absolute throughput numbers are not the AOT design point

## Open questions tracked on #189

Why does clean handle 6.9k RPS while vs collapses at 5-6k when they share the SAME 500-connection pool ceiling? Probably a connection-lifecycle difference between `IAsyncDbConnection`-direct (vs) and `IOrderRepository`-wrapped (clean). Next investigation step in #189: a connection-lifecycle micro-bench measuring connection acquire-to-release duration per template.

## Files

- `docs/benchmarks/2026-06-08-189-dotnet-counters-vs.md` — findings doc
- Raw counter CSVs from the 5k and 8k captures
- (any analysis script)
- `docs/benchmarks/README.md` index updated

## Why `chore:` and not `docs:`

This is investigation artifact, not user-facing documentation. `chore:` keeps release-please from cutting another patch release for what is internal bench data.

items.title: fix(routing): disable DML text routing — GQA logits wrong on-device (#91)
items.body:
## Context
Deep-dive on #91. The parity harness proved the **DML GQA decoder computes wrong logits on the Series S GPU** — and always has: throughput was benched, correctness never.

## Probe matrix (all on-device, deterministic)
| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| fp16 GQA / int4 GQA vs golden | NMSE ~1, top1 ` the`, seq=1 pure noise |
| `ORT_DISABLE_ALL` / `ep.dml.disable_graph_fusion` | **bit-identical** garbage |
| GenAI DLL rebuilt with graph capture disabled | **bit-identical** garbage |
| Same weights on CPU EP | ✅ top1 ` Paris`, overlap 0.90–1.00 |
| SD-Turbo (plain ORT, no GQA) on same device | ✅ correct |
| Forced-MHA build | loads on DML; GenAI 0.14 can't allocate non-share-buffer KV on DML (0-length first-step buffer) |
| `disable_metacommands` | provider option unreachable via GenAI's DML1 registration; DirectML 1.15.4 is the last release |

**Conclusion:** the corruption is in the DML GQA execution path on this driver/device, below every config- or DLL-reachable knob.

## Change
- `routing_policy.h`: `kDmlTextLogitsBroken` forces the CPU model in every routing mode (Auto/GpuOnly). One-flag flip to re-enable, gated on `scripts/validate-logit-parity.sh` PASS.
- `validate-console.sh` §2: asserts the gate holds (no GPU-routed text turn).
- Tests updated; pre-#91 GPU expectations kept under `doctest::skip` for the flip.
- README / technical-report / CHANGELOG document the finding honestly (prior GPU text numbers were real throughput on degraded output).

Diffusion (validated correct) stays on the GPU.

items.title: Add Autonomous Memory Engine core: wire protocol, TCP gateway, temporal log, context compiler, and benchmarks
items.body:
### Motivation
- Implement a high-throughput, low-allocation memory engine for autonomous agent swarms that communicates over a compact binary wire protocol via raw TCP pipelines.
- Provide a deterministic, token-bounded context compiler and an in-memory repository for fast recency/semantic retrieval to serve ContextQuery requests.
- Enable non-blocking ingestion and background indexing with a temporal log and a vector indexing worker to decouple network IO from indexing.
- Ship a self-contained benchmark harness to validate throughput and latency at scale and to document observed performance in the README.

### Description
- Add `AutonomousMemoryEngine` project with a `BinaryWireProtocol` implementing frame parsing/serialization, UTF-8 decoding, and message readers for `StateAppend`, `ContextQuery`, and `MemoryEvict`.
- Add `ContextCompiler` and `MemoryRepository` for simple recency/semantic scoring and deterministic packing of results against a hard token budget.
- Add `TemporalLog` with bounded `Channel`-based ingestion and `VectorIndexingWorker` `BackgroundService` that indexes incoming entries into the repository without blocking network threads.
- Add `TcpPipelineGateway` `BackgroundService` that accepts TCP connections, uses `System.IO.Pipelines` to parse frames zero-copy, dispatches frames to the log/compiler, and writes responses back to clients.
- Add `MemoryEngine.Benchmarks` project and `Program.cs` to simulate multi-connection ingestion and ContextQuery round-trips, plus a self-host helper to run the gateway + worker for local verification.
- Update `README.md` to describe the architecture, protocol framing, usage, and to include benchmark results and quick-start instructions.

### Testing
- Built the solutions with `dotnet build` for `AutonomousMemoryEngine` and `MemoryEngine.Benchmarks`, and the builds completed successfully.
- Ran the included benchmark harness via `dotnet run --project MemoryEngine.Benchmarks -- --self-host <port>` to exercise the full in-process gateway + worker end-to-end and validate frame handling.
- The benchmark run completed without socket exceptions or dropped frames and printed throughput and latency percentiles consistent with the numbers documented in `README.md`.
- No unit test suite was added in this change; validation consisted of the project builds and the end-to-end benchmark run described above.

items.title: feat(dfu): app-side armer — stage validation, extents, rollback snapshot, trial confirm (#619)
items.body:
S4 of the SD-staged DFU epic: the app-side armer. Find + validate a staged `UPDATE.BIN`, resolve it to raw block extents, snapshot the running image for rollback, arm the boot-state page, reboot into `obc-boot`; and on the other side of the reboot, confirm the trial boot at the health anchor. No UI screens (S5), no BLE (S6). The on-glass gate is driven over the debug VCOM harness via a new `dfu-install` command — exact recipe below.

## Design

**Request flow (the create-route drain shape).** The `dfu-install` VCOM command posts the *same app-level one-shot* the S5 menu entry will post (`App::request_dfu_install`). The ride loop drains it once per pass under the store lock — exclusive `Storage` + `RramSettingsStore` access — and refuses it mid-recording, over a pending ride save (RAM state a reboot would lose), or card-less. On success the drain never returns (reset); on failure the typed error has already streamed and the loop keeps riding.

**Where the pure logic lives: `obc_dfu::armer`** (new module, host-tested with mocks in `obc-dfu/tests/armer.rs`, mirroring the `engine`/`obc-boot` split):
- `scan(StageIo)` — the full validation matrix: header decode, size gates, the **full CRC-32 pass** over the image body, the whole-file extent chain (spec §2.3 — the chain includes the 64-byte header; `len`/`crc32` stay raw-image values, exactly what S3's engine consumes).
- `arm(ArmIo)` — the sequencing: rollback snapshot strictly **before** the page write, generation = old page + 1, the first-install/`installed:None` skip, totality over impossible page states.
- `confirm_trial` — `Trial{installed,..}` ⇒ `Idle{installed:Some}` + the header for the S5 toast.

The board side is thin adapters: `sd.rs` gets `dfu_scan_update` / `dfu_write_rollback` (`StageIo` over `SdByteSource` + `obc_platform::fat_extents::ExtentTable` — the map-extent machinery, plus a new `runs()` accessor), `settings.rs` gets `read_boot_state` (memory-mapped page decode, no buffer) / `write_boot_state` (the settings blob's 16-byte-line RRAMC idiom, compile-guarded alignment), and `src/dfu.rs` is the driver that wires them into `armer::arm` with watchdog pets between the long SD phases.

**Rollback snapshot.** `Idle{installed:Some(h)}` ⇒ the running image is read memory-mapped out of the app slot (`__app_slot_base`, a new linker-provided symbol — no hard-coded address) and written to `/ROLLBACK.BIN` as a full OBCU container (truncate-and-reuse, the `TRACK.OBT` idiom), then extent-resolved exactly like the update file. Two no-rollback paths, both surfaced: first-ever install (`installed:None`, dev-flashed), and a **running-mismatch guard** (slight extension beyond the issue): if the slot's bytes no longer CRC-match the installed record — an SWD reflash since the last install, a real dev workflow — snapshotting would record a rollback the bootloader must reject, so the arm proceeds with `rollback: None` and says so.

**Trial confirm anchor.** In `run_app`, at the **first successful `render_present`** — `main` mounts the SD and faults out before the loop can run, so "first frame presented AND SD mounted" both hold exactly there (no timer; the hardware watchdog #349 already converts a wedged boot into the rollback-triggering reset). The confirmed fact + version reach `obc-app` via `notify_update_confirmed`/`take_update_confirmed` — the `notify_warning` (#504) shape — for S5's one-time toast.

## Scan-error enum (`obc_dfu::ScanError`, surfaced verbatim)

`Missing` · `Truncated` (file shorter than `64 + image_len` — torn copy) · `BadHeader` (magic/version/header-CRC) · `BadCrc` (body CRC) · `Oversize` (`> MAX_IMAGE_LEN`) · `TooFragmented { extents }` (true count; fix = delete + re-copy) · `Io`. Each carries a stable `describe()` phrase; S5 reuses them as-is.

## Arm sequence + power-loss story

1. **Scan + validate** `UPDATE.BIN` — read-only. *Power cut: nothing happened.*
2. **Snapshot** `/ROLLBACK.BIN` + extent-resolve. *Power cut: an inert file on the card; nothing armed.*
3. **Compose `Armed` (gen = old+1) → one page write** — a single CRC-framed blob in whole 16-byte RRAMC lines; a torn write decodes to `Idle` (spec §2.4). *Power cut before: nothing happened; after: the install proceeds next boot — identical to the reset path (idempotent-`Armed`, invariant 2).*
4. **Beat (400 ms, flush the `D` status lines) → `SCB::sys_reset()`.** Nothing else sits between 3 and 4; a cut inside the beat *is* the armed-install path.

## RAM / stack

**No new resident statics on the default/`ble` builds.** The boot-state page is read memory-mapped (no 4 KB buffer); CRC/copy staging stays on `sd.rs`'s existing 512-byte-chunk idiom. `debug-uart` builds add one small static in `obc-platform`: the `D`-line channel + trigger signal (4×~100 B + a `Signal`, ≈0.5 KB, debug harness only). Transients, all in popped frames at the drain's shallow depth and never held across an `.await`: the decoded `BootState` (~1.7 KB), `StagedRef`s (~850 B each), the transient `ExtentTable` (~2.1 KB, unlike the map's session-long `.bss` table), and `write_boot_state`'s `EncodedPage` (~1.7 KB). The 256 KB-DK budget assert in `main.rs` is unchanged and passing on all three legs.

## Tests

- **Host, `obc-dfu/tests/armer.rs` (16):** scan matrix — missing / torn header / bad magic / header-CRC / body-CRC / oversize (gated before any bulk read) / truncated body / too-fragmented (both walls, true count carried) / io / happy (extents + CRC + header coherent); arm — **snapshot-before-page-write ordering asserted on the mock's call log**, generation bump (Idle→1, stale Armed 7→8), first-install no-snapshot, running-mismatch arms-without-rollback, failed snapshot aborts with the page untouched, failed page write reported; trial confirm — Trial→Idle round-trips the codec, Idle/Armed are no-ops.
- **Host, `obc-app`:** the DFU one-shots are take-once (the create-route contract). **Host, `obc-platform`:** `dfu-install` parse (exact-tag, case-sensitive, junk-tolerant).
- **Workspace:** `cargo test` green (76 suites), `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` green.
- **Board:** all three legs build + clippy clean — default, `--features debug-uart`, `--no-default-features --features ble` (the request drain compiles everywhere; `dfu-install` only rides `debug-uart`). Three-step fmt clean. `obc-boot` untouched (verified).

## Docs sync

`docs/` untouched by design — the DFU concept page is S8 (#623). For S8 to pick up: the update pipeline now has its app side (armer flow, `ROLLBACK.BIN`, the trial confirm anchor) — this PR's README additions (`firmware/README.md` §Firmware update images tail, board README §`dfu-install`) are the interim build/run reference and can seed that page. Nothing existing in `docs/content/` describes DFU yet, so nothing went stale.

Part of #615, closes #619.

## On-glass gate — the recipe (owner)

Prereqs once: `obc-boot` flashed at `0x0` (`cd firmware/obc-boot && cargo run --release` — flash-twice quirk applies), VCOM HWFC off, card in.

**Two-version loop (A→B, then B→A):**

```sh
# 1. Build + flash vA (this branch), note its banner hash.
cd firmware/obc-fw-nrf54l
cargo run --release --features debug-uart          # flash twice if the first fails
# RTT shows:  obc-fw-nrf54l 0.1.0+<gitA>

# 2. Build vB = any other commit (e.g. develop HEAD, or a whitespace commit on this branch),
#    wrap it, stage it on the card (card in a reader; UPDATE.BIN in the ROOT, 8.3, no LFN):
cargo objcopy --release --features debug-uart -- -O binary app.bin
cd .. && cargo run -p obc-mkimage -- wrap --bin obc-fw-nrf54l/app.bin \
    --version "$(git describe --always --dirty)" --out /Volumes/<CARD>/UPDATE.BIN
# sanity: cargo run -p obc-mkimage -- inspect /Volumes/<CARD>/UPDATE.BIN

# 3. Card back in, boot vA, attach logs + trigger over the VCOM:
cd obc-fw-nrf54l && cargo rtt --features debug-uart   # same features or it re-flashes!
# second terminal:
PORT=/dev/tty.usbmodem<...>            # the J-Link CDC port
stty -f "$PORT" 115200 raw -echo
cat "$PORT" &                          # watch the D-lines
printf 'dfu-install\n' > "$PORT"
```

Expected: `D scanning UPDATE.BIN (running <gitA>)` → `D scan ok: <verB> (N B, k extent(s))` → `D rollback snapshot written to ROLLBACK.BIN` → `D armed gen=G -- rebooting into the bootloader` → reset → **S3's LED sequence** (short pulse, slow-blink verify, fast-blink flash/readback, reset) → device returns, RTT banner `obc-fw-nrf54l 0.1.0+<gitB>` → on the first presented frame: `dfu: trial confirmed — running <verB> is now the installed image` (that line *is* the `Idle{installed:vB}` write). Then repeat steps 2–3 with vA's `UPDATE.BIN` to prove B→A; the second arm's `rollback snapshot written` line also proves the confirm left `Idle{installed:Some}`.

**Kill-power pass (idempotent-`Armed`):** trigger a third install; when the LED goes fast-blink (flash pass — after slow-blink verify), cut power. Repower: the bootloader re-enters `Armed`, the whole verify→flash→readback pass reruns from scratch, and the device comes up as the staged version. Nothing to clean up.

**Throughput numbers (S3's deferred measurement):** for one of the passes, flash `obc-boot` built with `--features rtt` and capture its DWT verify/flash/readback wall-time + KiB/s lines, plus the end-to-end wall time (copy→armed→flashed→confirmed) — the acceptance number this PR should report back into #615.

If anything rejects: the `D install failed (…)` line carries the typed reason verbatim; a bad stage costs nothing (state page untouched, old app keeps riding).
