items.title: perf: retune the upload pipeline for the sEMMC card
items.body:
Map uploads over the cable run at ~1 MB/s while the card underneath writes at 8.2 MB/s. The pipeline that carries them was tuned in the SPI era, when the card itself did 1.07 MB/s, and it is serial and single-buffered from the browser to the FAT. This is the full retune.

**Everything below is a prediction, not a measurement.** Nothing here has been on glass. The bench checklist at the bottom is what turns these into numbers.

## Review round (2 majors, 2 fork bugs, 9 minors)

An adversarial review came back with no criticals. Everything below is fixed and pushed; each fix
was checked by re-introducing the bug and watching the new test fail.

**M1 — the abort stray-byte window.** Real, and this branch made it 8× wider. First fix drained on
all four early-termination paths; **round 2 established that was wrong on three of them** and it was
redesigned — see below.

**M2 — the commit widening was global.** Also real. `commitTimeoutMs(commitBytes ?? src.totalLen)`
applied to *every* upload, so a route or an `UPDATE.BIN` went 15 s → 60 s and a wedged device took
4–40× longer to surface. It is opt-in now: no `commitBytes`, no change. The set manifest is the only
caller that sets it. **The plain-map commit deliberately does not get it** — `Storage::
map_upload_commit` is a close, an open, a 40-byte header read, a 4-byte write and a flush, which the
default budget covers with room to spare. A new `committing` phase ("Finishing on the device") names
the wait on screen, raised through a new `onSent` hook; the set path already had "sealing map", a
plain map had nothing.

**Fork patch — both bugs confirmed and fixed.** These mattered most.

* **m10, write order.** `update_fat(prev, first)` ran before `write_chain_run` — the inverse of
  upstream's crash-safe order, leaving a chain pointing at clusters the FAT still reported free.
  Swapped. The one-block cache never forced it: `write_chain_run` writes back before returning.
* **m11, `run.max(1)`.** A cluster the FAT said was taken was chained anyway. It is an
  `AllocationError` now, and the early return that skipped the read for a run of one is gone, so the
  entry is always verified.

Both are pinned. `the_run_is_written_before_the_link_that_points_at_it` reads the recorded write
order with no filesystem geometry. The refusal is unreachable through `VolumeManager` — the scan and
the run measurement read the same FAT through the same cache — so it is unit-tested beside the
function, and the integration test that carried its name is renamed to what it actually covers.

**Minors.** m3 (a queued write carried no rejection handler until `retireOldest` reached it — a
throwaway `.catch` at queue time, real `await` unchanged), m4 (the comment claiming `allSettled`
lets `reset()` clear the OUT half was false on the cancel path; it now describes the safe behaviour),
m5 (`ARCHITECTURE_RESOURCE_BASELINE.md` entry for the re-pin and the two new report rows), m6 (the
feature's `E0599` is now documented in both places — a cargo feature cannot assert a dependency's
API, so nothing warns), m7 (`report_cluster_size` reads the MBR + BPB at mount and either confirms
`STAGE_HALF_LEN` is one cluster or warns with both numbers), m9 (five new host tests), m12 (0.68 →
0.72 MB/s, MiB in a decimal-MB document), m13 (`stage.rs` no longer claims BLE shares the stage —
only the USB plane does), m8 (the progress card is documented as a liveness indicator, not a commit
count).

Nothing was rejected as wrong. One correction to a test claim I would rather state than bury: the
m3 regression test needed a hand-rolled pipe rather than a `vi.spyOn` — a spy records what it
returns, which attaches a handler to a rejected promise and hides the exact thing under test. With
the spy it passed either way; with the hand-rolled pipe it fails without the `.catch`.

## Merged up to develop (#1170, terrain shard)

The terrain wire fix touches the same classifier, spec section and loopback. Independent changes —
terrain adds an *object type*, this adds an *abort disposition* — but adjacent, so resolved by hand.
The combination creates one case neither branch wrote and which is now covered: **an idle `op = 3`
naming `terrainShard` is a quiesce**, so it deletes nothing, which is what #1170's `forget_terrain`
semantics want. `finish_idle_abort`'s other half only drops `/routes/UPLOAD.TMP`, and terrain streams
straight into `MS{id}.OBD`, so a quiesce cannot reach the raster either. `loopback.ts` puts
`clearStagedSet()` behind the `mapSet` key with `terrainShard` on the quiesce arm, and there is a new
e2e test for a terrain-bearing set surviving a quiesce. Spec rule 5 → 6 after #1170's insertion, with
every cross-reference corrected.

## Post-review cleanup

The fork patch landed upstream, so the scaffolding is deleted: patch file, `sdmmc-prealloc` feature,
and the CI gate that cloned and replayed it. Pre-allocation is simply on. Details in the `(d)`
section above.

## Review round 4 — the closing round

Round 3's protocol redesign was confirmed correct on both ends. Two mechanical holes remained, and
they share a character worth naming: **the fix looked right and did not run.**

### MAJOR-A — the late-`aborted` "drop" dropped nothing

`Mailbox.tryTake` splices out *only matches*, and `Mailbox.take` is an unfiltered FIFO `shift()`. So
narrowing the predicate stopped the stale message matching and left it queued — and the next
`awaitTransferResult` handed it back as the current upload's terminal result. Same spurious failure
one step later, now as `aborted`, which `sendAssembledSetFile` does **not** retry (only
`crc-mismatch`). A set upload would die outright on a verdict the device never issued about it.

Both readers consume and discard now: `checkUploadOpen` loops past stale `aborted`s and stops only on
a terminal failure; `awaitTransferResult` skips them on the blocking path, sharing the caller's
budget rather than restarting it, with `expectAborted` for the two callers that legitimately want one.
Test injects a late `aborted` mid-upload and asserts the upload still commits — **verified to fail
with "The upload was aborted" without the fix.**

### MAJOR-B — the manifest quiesce had zero coverage

The `mapSet` → `mapShard` rewrite in `sendQuiesceAbort` is the only thing keeping the original
set-deleting CRITICAL from reappearing on the *manifest* path: a refused manifest is announced as
`mapSet`, so its quiesce would name `mapSet` and abandon the set it is about to re-send. Deleting the
rewrite left all 863 tests green. The new e2e test — manifest refused once with `crcMismatch`, set
survives, retry commits — **fails with "The device does not have that object" without it**, because
the loopback answers a `mapSet` descriptor with `notFound` once the shards are gone.

### Drift minors (C–G, I)

Four comments stated the **inverse** of the rule they document — the exact class that let the original
bug through. `write.ts`'s commit budget (a timed-out manifest wait no longer deletes the set; the
honest cost is reporting failure for a map that landed), `abandonMapSet`'s doc, `drain_bulk_out`'s
"only two places" (`run_echo` made it three), and `DRAIN_BUDGET_MS`'s rationale (which asserted
exactly MAJOR-A's non-behaviour). `sendAbort`'s doc block, orphaned onto `sendQuiesceAbort` last
round, is re-homed. Spec §4.2 now says draining is correct at "the abort handshake, with or without a
transfer in flight" rather than only the idle case. The patches README's `git push` gained its remote.

### Accepted, with reasons recorded in the code

* **H** — `report_cluster_size` no longer claims to mirror `fat_extents.rs` wholesale. That one
  refuses a superfloppy card outright because it builds extents the ride path depends on; this one
  reports its cluster size because it is a boot log line. A card the volume manager cannot mount
  never reaches an upload, so leniency here costs nothing.
* **J** — the quiesce's rewritten shard id can name a part the set does not have. Harmless: an idle
  abort's descriptor selects *which cleanup*, and the quiesce does none — the device never looks the
  part up.
* **K** — the echo abort arm races only the OUT read, so a host that stopped reading could still park
  the loop in `ep_in.write`. Echo is a bring-up harness driven by a host that is always draining, and
  the endpoint teardown is the backstop. The upload path — the one a rider hits — races at every
  await.

## Review round 3 — the abort's two meanings

Round 2 shipped a **regression**, and verification caught it. Making the host's abort unconditional
gave `op = 3` a second meaning the device could not see, and the cost was a rider's whole map.

### CRITICAL — a refused shard deleted the set

```
shard crcMismatch → withTransferSlot catch → op=3 naming the shard
                  → device: nothing in flight → set_upload_abort (unconditional on USB)
                  → every file of the set deleted
                  → sendAssembledSetFile re-sends that one shard into an empty set
                  → the manifest's cross-check fails
```

It contradicted the design the data plane documents ("a failed shard drops only itself") and made the
manifest's own CRC retry unable to ever succeed. Before round 2, the `transferClosed` skip is what
had kept the set alive.

**The proposed key was wrong on the facts, and I fixed the cause rather than applying it.**
`abandonMapSet` was sending `type: MapShard` — byte-identical to the quiesce after a refused shard —
so keying the device on `MapSet` alone would have silently disabled set abandonment and left
gigabytes staged (the bug #1039 fixed). Both ends move instead:

| | descriptor | meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `abandonMapSet()` | `mapSet` | abandon the staged set |
| failure-path quiesce | anything else (`sendQuiesceAbort` rewrites a set-shaped one) | drain the pipe, touch nothing |

`classify_transfer` abandons only for `mapSet`, and its cleanup moved out into `finish_idle_abort` so
the transport sequences it — on USB that is **drain first, delete second**, which is the ordering
`DRAIN_BUDGET_MS` already claimed and MAJOR-3 pointed out was not happening.

### MAJOR-2 — a latched `DRAIN_REQ`

It is the first arm of the idle `select` and nothing cleared it: not the timeout path, not the
endpoint-lost teardown (which resets `TRANSFER_ARM`/`TRANSFER_ABORT` beside it). A cable dying between
the signal and the select left it standing, and the next enumeration's first upload opened straight
into a drain. Reset in both places. The same handshake could also answer ahead of itself — a
timed-out-then-completed request left a `DONE` standing that satisfied the *next* request's wait — so
requests are numbered and completions echo the number. +8 B, re-pinned.

### MAJOR-1 — the negative check was hollow, and the mock was why

`LoopbackPipe.reset()` cleared **both** directions, so host→device bytes vanished on every failure —
and `withTransferSlot` calls `resetBulk()` on every failure. That models WebUSB backwards: `reset()`
there is `clearHalt`, which cancels no transfer and un-queues no byte. It clears only `inbound` now.
With the corrected mock, removing the quiesce abort fails the stray-byte test with a real
`crcMismatch` — which is what it always claimed to check.

### The e2e test

`flows.test.ts`'s existing shard-retry test stubs `client.upload` with `vi.fn()`, so it could not see
an abort, a descriptor type, or what the device did with the set — it passed throughout the
regression. The new one drives the real client against the loopback: two shards, the second refused
once with `crcMismatch`, then the manifest; it asserts the set still holds both shards and that the
manifest commits. **Verified to fail (`expected 1 to be 2`) when the device abandons on a
shard-shaped abort.**

### Spec — the load-bearing part

The wire contract had one meaning of an idle `op = 3` and not the other, which is how this got past
review: the code was doing something no document described. `obc-ble-interface-spec.md` §5 rule 5 now
distinguishes abandonment (`mapSet`) from quiesce (everything else) with the reasoning; §4.2 gains
the idle-abort drain rule — what it is for, that it is the *only* point where draining is correct,
that a device MUST NOT drain on its own terminations, and that it MUST bound it; the storage-full
paragraph stops claiming a CoC reset is the recovery on a transport with no channel to reopen; and
two consequential lines (atomicity, Resume) are qualified. `companion-link.md` gains the same idea in
the reader's terms.

### Round-3 minors

`report_cluster_size` now mirrors `obc-storage`'s own correct MBR/VBR discrimination (signature **and**
`BPB_BytsPerSec == 512` **and** non-zero `BPB_SecPerClus`) — my earlier commit message claimed a
signature check that was not there, and a signature check alone would have been wrong anyway since a
superfloppy VBR carries `0xAA55` too. `run_echo` gained an abort arm (it stopped being free once every
failure is followed by `op = 3`). `checkUploadOpen` no longer takes a late `aborted` as the next
upload's rejection — `statuses.drain()` runs at slot *entry*, so it never cleared it, contrary to what
a comment claimed. The `DRAIN_BUDGET_MS` doc's inverted fallback claim is corrected. The fork-gate
steps get `timeout-minutes: 10`, and the `Cargo.lock` restore moved into its own `if: always()` step —
inside a `run:` under `bash -e` it was skipped exactly when it was needed. The `abandonMapSet`
double-abort (minor f) dissolves: the second one is now a quiesce.

## Review round 2 — the drain, redesigned

Round 1's drain was verified correct on M2, m3 and both fork-patch bugs (mutation-tested on a
scratch fork). M1 came back **incomplete, and needing a rethink rather than a bigger budget**. Both
findings were right.

**Where the peer is quiet is the whole question**, and I had not asked it. Draining an endpoint the
host is *still pumping into* is not a drain — it discards exactly as fast as the host refills, and
the one thing that would make the host stop, the terminal `transferResult`, was sitting behind the
drain. On a device-originated termination that bought up to 750 ms of delay before the host could
learn to stop, plus a warn on every large upload that hit a storage failure. Removed from all three
such paths, with a comment saying why, because they read like they need one. They never needed it:
the host's send loop settles every outstanding write before it unwinds, and the idle loop is reading
throughout.

**The abort handshake is the moment, and it has two shapes.** The host has thrown out of its send
loop, holds an `op = 3` open, and will not send another descriptor until it is answered.

1. *Abort against a live transfer* — already drained; now drains **before** `discard_upload` rather
   than after, so the endpoint goes quiet while a set's shard deletes are still running instead of
   behind them, and the arena's staging arm is not held across it. That also makes the budget
   arithmetic honest (the minor about `DRAIN_BUDGET_MS`).
2. *Abort with nothing armed* — the hole. A descriptor-level reject answers from `classify_transfer`
   and never arms the data plane, so a host that notices it and aborts before retrying hit a path
   with no drain at all. Now `TransferDisposition::AnswerIdleAbort`, split from `Answer` because it
   is the one disposition carrying a transport-side obligation: the USB control plane asks the data
   plane (which owns the endpoint) to drain, waits, then answers. BLE treats it as a plain `Answer` —
   its CoC is closed and reopened around a failed exchange, which *is* the discard.

**The host had to change too, and this is the half that actually closes it.** `withTransferSlot`
skipped the abort whenever a terminal result had already been consumed. What the handshake buys here
is the *endpoint*, not the gate — so the abort is unconditional on the failure path now. The device's
discard-while-idle is a race against the next descriptor, not a guarantee; **the loopback test
demonstrates exactly that**, failing without the unconditional abort. `transferClosed` had no readers
left and is deleted rather than kept as decoration.

The loopback grew the two device behaviours these tests turn on — discarding bulk bytes while nothing
is armed (with arming taking the channel back, as `TRANSFER_ARM` does) and draining before answering
an idle abort. Without them it modelled a channel that quietly accumulates unclaimed bytes, which is
a failure mode the real device does not have.

**Cost: 184 B resident**, itemised by symbol diff (`llvm-nm`) in
`firmware/docs/ARCHITECTURE_RESOURCE_BASELINE.md`: +160 on the USB task's `TaskStorage` (a third
select arm, and the control plane's await), +24 for two `Signal`s, −37 of merged-globals churn, +37
of section alignment. Poll frame, task body and `.uninit` unmoved; residual stack 77,272 → 77,088 B,
still 2.1× the 35,808 B measured deep-ride peak.

### Round-2 minors

`DRAIN_BUDGET_MS`'s comment now tells the whole story (the shard deletes share the host's abort-ack
budget, and the drain is sequenced first so they do not stack); `report_cluster_size` checks the
`0x55AA` boot signature before trusting a partition LBA, so a superfloppy card no longer produces a
confidently wrong warning; `onSent` is guarded, because a throwing hook would have unwound into the
abort path against a transfer being committed; the manifest's CRC retry resets the phase off
`committing` before re-sending; the progress test now measures against what the transport has
accepted rather than asserting monotonicity that held either way; `OBCA_Spec.md` no longer carries a
board-specific measured figure; the README figure is back to **~0.68 MB/s** with the convention named
(`lib/format.ts` treats `1 << 20` as "MB" everywhere the app shows a rate, so that is what the
harness's own bar reports).

**The prealloc CI gate is in**, not deferred as accepted risk: the `embedded` job clones the fork,
`git am`s every patch in `firmware/patches/`, runs the fork's suite, and type-checks
`--features sdmmc-prealloc` against it through a command-line `[patch]` override, restoring
`Cargo.lock` afterwards (the override re-resolves, and every other step is `--locked`). Verified by
running the exact sequence locally.

Branch is merged up to `origin/develop`. One conflict, resolved in develop's favour: #1167 had landed
the same `sd_bounce` / `semmc_driver` report rows independently.

## Before / after

```
BEFORE
  browser   [ 16 KB transferOut ]──idle──[ 16 KB ]──idle──[ 16 KB ]
                                    ^ renderer→USB-service round trip, one in flight
  device    ep.read 512 B ×32  ──────────────────────────► stage 16 KB
  card                                        └─ CMD25 (16 KB, split by cluster)
  FAT           + 4 single-block writes per 32 KB cluster, interleaved
                                     ▲ each one a whole program cycle

AFTER
  browser   [64 KB][64 KB][64 KB][64 KB]  ← up to 4 in flight, retire-one-queue-one
  device    ep.read 512 B ×64  ──► half A          half B ──► ep.read continues
  card                              └─ CMD25, exactly one 32 KiB cluster, no partial ends
  FAT       chain reserved at the announce: ~4 single-block writes per 4 MiB
```

## What is in here, and what each part is honestly worth

| Lever | State | Predicted effect |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| (b) host pipelining — 4 in-flight `transferOut`s, 64 KiB chunks | **done** | large; removes a per-chunk round trip from the critical path |
| (d) FAT pre-allocation | **done and on** | large; **511 → 1** single-block writes per 256 KiB in the write path, measured on the fork's RAM disk |
| (e) `STAGE_LEN` re-sweep — 16 KiB → 2 × 32 KiB | **done** | moderate; each flush is now exactly one cluster / one CMD25 |
| (a) double-buffered stage | **done** | **~0 today.** Structural. See below. |
| (c) multiple packets per `ep.read` | **not possible** — upstream blocker | would be large; this is what makes (a) real |
| commit-wait robustness fix | **done** | prevents losing a successfully committed set |
| abort-path endpoint drain (review M1, redesigned in round 2) | **done** | closes the spurious-retry-failure window the wider host window opened |

### (a) and (c) are the same problem, and (c) is blocked upstream

The task asked for the flush to overlap reception instead of NAKing through it. It cannot, today, and the reason is worth stating precisely because it is not a bug to fix here:

* `Semmc::write_blocks` is synchronous and busy-polls `wait_completion`. That is **deliberate** — the function's own doc explains at length why a `WFE` sleep is unsound on this part. So a card write burns the one thread-mode CPU for its whole duration, and on a cooperative executor nothing else runs, including the USB endpoint's software re-arm.
* Reception during a flush is therefore bounded by what the USBHS core buffers on its own. That is exactly **one** max packet: `embassy-usb-synopsys-otg` 0.4 `EndpointOut::read` re-arms with `set_pktcnt(1)` and `set_xfrsiz(max_packet_size)`, and the driver's per-endpoint staging buffer is one `max_packet_size`. Both are hardcoded, and the endpoint's max packet is the same number the descriptor publishes, so it cannot be raised without a fork of that crate.

So the halves are shipped as the *structure* overlap needs, and `Stage::drain` is the one function that becomes a future the day the sEMMC transfer grows an awaitable completion. The code and the module doc both say this rather than implying a win. Two follow-ups worth filing: an awaitable sEMMC completion, and either a fork of `embassy-usb-synopsys-otg` or an upstream PR to let a driver arm more than one packet.

What (a) *does* buy today is real but small: the transport never has to wait behind a flush partway through a host chunk, and it made the cluster-sized flush safe to take.

### (d) — pre-allocation, and the fork

`embedded-sdmmc` comes from `timohueser/embedded-sdmmc-rs` via `[patch.crates-io]`, in two resolve
roots. There was no pre-allocation API and none reachable from the app side, so this needed a fork
change — which is why earlier revisions of this PR shipped a patch file, a feature flag and a CI gate
that replayed the patch. **Timo has pushed it** (`e846db66`), so all of that is gone: both
`Cargo.lock`s pin the new rev, the `sdmmc-prealloc` feature is deleted rather than defaulted (it
existed only to bridge a state that no longer exists), and the ordinary `--locked` build legs
exercise the real dependency — a stronger gate than the scaffolding was. Net −1,014 lines.

Before deleting anything I verified the pushed commit: parent exactly `4cada7b3`, and its tree
byte-identical to the patch applied on that parent (`git am` onto the base, then diff the trees —
empty). Fork suite green at that rev.

What it does: `VolumeManager::preallocate` on top of `FatVolume::alloc_cluster_run`, which chains a
run of consecutive free clusters inside **one** FAT block and writes that block back once. Today's
`alloc_cluster` costs four single-block writes per cluster (`update_fat` twice, each mirrored across
both FATs); a FAT32 block holds 128 entries, so 4 MiB of file now costs what 32 KiB used to. Its own
test, on the fork's RAM-disk image: writing 256 KiB leaves **511 → 1** single-block writes in the
write path, byte-identical read-back. Two crash-safety properties each have a test that fails without
them: the run's entries are written before the link that points at them, and a run never starts on an
entry the FAT says is taken.

**Cost of turning it on: +1,968 B of flash, 0 B of everything else** — the fork's allocator plus our
call sites, code LTO stripped while `upload_reserve` was a stub. Resident, `.uninit`, poll frame, task
body and residual stack are byte-identical on both profiles; a reservation is a burst of FAT writes at
the open, not state the device holds.

### The robustness fix### The robustness fix

The terminal wait of an upload shared `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000` with every register read. Committing a volume-set **manifest** — a file under 2 KB — re-opens and cross-checks every shard header already on the card (`Storage::set_manifest_commit` → `set_shard_totals`), behind a card that may still be finishing the previous shard's program cycle. On timeout the client throws *and* `withTransferSlot` fires an `op = 3` abort, and the device answers that by **deleting the whole set** — including one it may have just committed successfully. That is data loss, not a slow spinner.

The commit wait is now `commitTimeoutMs()`: 60 s + 200 ms per megabyte the device has to re-read, capped at 10 minutes. `TransferOptions.commitBytes` is how the set path tells it the manifest's commit is priced against the *set*, not the manifest.

## Expected throughput — the reasoning

The pipeline is strictly serial (see (a) above), so per staged cluster the cost is `t_usb + t_card + t_fat`, and throughput is `32 KiB / that`.

* **`t_fat` is the biggest single term today and it goes to ~0.** Four single-block writes per 32 KiB cluster, each a full program cycle. Even at a generous 1.5 ms per cycle that is 6 ms per cluster — on its own a 5.3 MB/s ceiling, before any data has moved. Pre-allocation takes it to ~4 writes per 4 MiB, i.e. ~0.05 ms amortised per cluster.
* **`t_card` improves modestly.** 32 KiB at 8.2 MB/s is ~4 ms, and a cluster-aligned flush means one CMD25 of 64 blocks rather than a split with partial ends.
* **`t_usb` improves a lot in the tail.** 64 KiB per chunk with 4 outstanding means the endpoint is fed continuously; what remains is the per-packet interrupt + re-arm cost, 64 packets per staged half.

If the per-packet cost is ~10 µs, `t_usb` ≈ 0.65 ms per 32 KiB and the serial sum is ~4.7 ms →
**~7 MB/s**. If it is ~40 µs (a re-arm that misses its microframe), `t_usb` ≈ 2.6 ms and the sum is
~6.6 ms → **~5 MB/s**.

**So: ~5–7 MB/s, against today's ~1 MB/s — a 3–5× improvement.** That is the number this PR is for,
and every lever is live in it: host pipelining, the cluster-sized double-buffered stage, and FAT
pre-allocation. The residual ceiling is the per-packet receive cost — lever (c), the one blocked
upstream by `embassy-usb-synopsys-otg`'s hardcoded single-packet re-arm.

**It is a prediction, not a measurement.** Nothing here has been on glass. The bench checklist below
is what turns it into a number.

## Anchors that differed from the diagnosis## Anchors that differed from the diagnosis

* **`BOUNCE_BLOCKS` is a non-issue on this path.** The arena is `#[repr(C, align(8))]` and the fork's fast path takes `&buffer[written..]` at multiples of 4, so the staged write is always 4-aligned and never bounces. Left alone; raising it would cost `.bss` 1:1 against a case that does not fire. `warn_bounce` firing on glass would mean something else regressed — it is on the bench checklist for that reason.
* **The map path was already on 32 KiB chunks**, not the 16 KiB `DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE`: `write.ts` had its own `MAP_CHUNK`. It is deleted, so there is one dial.
* **`ep.read` cannot be widened** (lever (c)) — hardcoded upstream, detailed above.
* **The flush's 17 ms/16 KB pricing** in `stage.rs` was an SPI-era in-code estimate that was never re-measured; it is now marked as historical rather than carried forward as fact.
* **Pre-existing red found in passing:** `resource_guard.py report` has been failing "missing entries: sd_bounce, semmc_driver" since the sEMMC pivot — the baseline pinned two rows the report table never grew. Fixed here (four lines in `main.rs`) because it blocked re-pinning `arena_usb`; `semmc_driver` was also 8 B stale (52 → 44).

## Resource impact: none

`arena_usb` 16,384 → 65,536 B and **nothing else moved**, because the arena is `max(arms)` and the render arm is 117,408 B. Measured locally against the same tree with the halves back at 16 KiB:

| | before | after |
| :-- | --: | --: |
| `.bss + .data` | 295,816 B | 295,816 B |
| `.uninit` | 118,432 B | 118,432 B |
| largest guarded poll frame | 9,728 B | 9,728 B |
| residual main stack | 77,272 B | 77,272 B |

Round 2's drain redesign adds **+184 B** on top (296,000 B resident, residual stack 77,088 B) —
itemised by symbol diff in the entry above. `resource_guard.py board` and `report` pass on **both**
profiles. The human-readable entries are in `firmware/docs/ARCHITECTURE_RESOURCE_BASELINE.md`.

## On-glass bench checklist

**Measure MB/s from the browser console.** Open the builder's device tab with the console open and send a map; the client reports settled bytes, so:

```js
// paste before starting the send
performance.mark('obc-start');
// after the transfer completes, with the map's byte length:
const ms = performance.now() - performance.getEntriesByName('obc-start')[0].startTime;
console.log((BYTES / 1e6) / (ms / 1000), 'MB/s');
```

The device also prints its own figure at the end of every transfer over RTT, which is the authority because it excludes the browser's CRC pass:

```
usb: [bulk] upload finished: id N -> committed (X bytes in Y ms, ~Z kB/s)
```

**Watch for on RTT (`cargo rtt`, matching `--features`):**

* `SD: misaligned block buffer at 0x… — bouncing (throughput cost)` — `warn_bounce`. Must **not** appear. If it does, the staged write lost its alignment and every flush is going out as 2 KiB CMD25s.
* `usb: [bulk] no staging arm granted — streaming unstaged (slower, never wrong)` — the ride loop refused the arena arm and the upload is running at the ~0.2 MB/s per-packet path. Any measurement taken after this line is meaningless.
* `SD: reserved N cluster(s) for a M B upload` — once per upload, at the open. Its absence means `preallocate` refused and the chain is growing the old way; the warn line beside it says why, and the transfer is still correct, just slower.
* `SD: 32768 B clusters — one upload staging half is exactly one cluster` — printed once at mount.
  If it is the **warn** variant instead (`… against a 32768 B staging half — upload flushes are not
  one-cluster`), the card is formatted with a different cluster size and the throughput numbers below
  will not match; reformat, or sweep `STAGE_HALF_LEN` to match the card.
* `usb: [bulk] drained N stray bytes the host had already queued` — expected after a cancel or a
  rejected transfer, and a good sign. It should appear only around an abort; anywhere else means the
  drain has crept back onto a path where the host is still pumping.
  `usb: [bulk] still receiving 750 ms into an abort drain` means the drain hit its ceiling — worth a
  look, though the retry still recovers.
* `usb: [ctl] idle abort — draining the bulk pipe before answering` — the descriptor-reject path
  doing its job.
* `sEMMC: completion seen without a VPR00 interrupt` — unrelated to this branch, but it changes what the timing means.

**Sweeping the constants:**

* Device stage: `usb::STAGE_HALF_LEN` (`src/usb/mod.rs`). One line, then re-pin `compile_time_allocations.arena_usb` to `2 × STAGE_HALF_LEN`. Useful rungs 16 K / 32 K / 64 K; it wants to track the card's cluster size, and the arena ceiling is ~117 KB for the *pair*.
* Host: `DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE` and `UPLOAD_WINDOW` (`builder/app/src/lib/usb/client.ts`). Bytes queued at the endpoint are their product (256 KiB today) — that is what has to cover a device-side flush.

**Also worth checking on glass:** that the map still redraws and the UI stays responsive during a transfer (the per-flush `yield_now` is the only thing guaranteeing the ride loop a turn, and there are now half as many of them per megabyte), and that an unplug mid-upload still discards cleanly.

## Docs

Landed as a separate `docs:` commit. The retune invalidated a dozen "the SD card is the bottleneck at high-hundreds of KB/s over the proven 8 MHz SPI" claims across the rider-visible copy, the public docs, the harness and the specs; the replacement deliberately names no rate, because nothing has been measured end to end. `companion-link.md` gains a **"What actually limits an upload"** section covering the four stages. `python3 docs/build_docs.py --check-links` passes.

## Note on `feat/usb-terrain-shard-1044`

Diffs in the shared files are kept surgical: `usb/data_plane.rs` gains one line inside the existing open block, `write.ts` two hunks, `client.ts` is additive plus one loop body swapped for a call. Happy to rebase after that branch merges.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: Add local model and hardware evaluation matrix for translation quality (#81)
items.body:
## Summary

Adds a repeatable framework for making evidence-based hardware and model-scaling decisions. Defines quantitative thresholds for quality and throughput bottlenecks so hardware upgrades are justified by benchmark data, not assumptions.

## Linked issue

Closes #81

## What changed

- **`docs/model-hardware-evaluation.md`** (new): Full decision-framework covering:
  - Three runtime profiles (`rtx_4090_24gb`, `ai_workstation_96gb`, `multi_node`) with hardware specs, max viable model sizes, and the `hardware_profile` metadata key for each
  - Five model tiers (7–8B dev, 14B, 32B, 70B-class, 405B+) with VRAM requirements and minimum profile needed
  - Sequenced prerequisite steps before any hardware expansion (benchmark corpus → direct LLM translation → QC → re-benchmark)
  - Quantitative quality bottleneck definition: BLEU < 45 **or** chrF < 65 **or** WER > 0.35 after prompt/QC tuning, with ≥ 2-point chrF improvement required to count a model upgrade as justified
  - Throughput bottleneck definition: > 4 h/episode, confirmed inference-bound via profiling
  - `benchmark_run` JSON schema for attaching hardware/model metadata to `benchmark_results.json`
  - Decision matrix mapping quality/throughput state to recommended action

- **`acceptance/81-model-hardware-evaluation.md`** (new): Acceptance criteria mapping for issue #81 with all criteria marked met; notes deferred code-level work (automatic `benchmark_run` embedding, `ai_workstation`/`multi_node` config profile values).

## Tests

- [ ] New tests added for new behavior
- [ ] Existing tests updated where behavior changed
- [ ] All tests pass locally (`pytest`)
- [x] If no tests apply, reason documented here: Documentation-only change; no executable code added.

## Acceptance checklist

- [x] Acceptance criteria for the linked issue are met — see `acceptance/81-model-hardware-evaluation.md`
- [x] `docs/` updated if architecture, module boundaries, or design decisions changed
- [ ] `specs/` updated or created if this implements a spec
- [ ] `prompts/` updated if this introduces or changes a reusable AI prompt
- [x] `acceptance/` updated if this changes or defines acceptance criteria for a feature

**Acceptance criteria status:**

See [`acceptance/81-model-hardware-evaluation.md`](acceptance/81-model-hardware-evaluation.md). All eight criteria met. Deferred: code-level `benchmark_run` metadata embedding in `benchmark_results.json`; `ai_workstation` and `multi_node` config profile values in `config.yaml`.

## AI usage disclosure

- [ ] AI tooling was NOT used for this change
- [x] AI tooling WAS used — details below:

**Tool(s) used:** GitHub Copilot coding agent

**What was generated:** Both new files (`docs/model-hardware-evaluation.md`, `acceptance/81-model-hardware-evaluation.md`) in full.

**How it was validated (tests run, diff reviewed, etc.):** Code review and CodeQL scan passed (documentation-only; no executable code). Content cross-checked against issue #81 acceptance criteria and existing project conventions (`acceptance/README.md`, `docs/architecture/adr-001-local-first-platform.md`, `config.yaml` profiles).

**Assumptions made by the AI that affect design or scope:** Quality thresholds (BLEU < 45, chrF < 65, WER > 0.35, ≥ 2-point chrF delta) and the 4 h/episode throughput threshold are proposed values; they should be validated against the real benchmark corpus once fixtures exist.

## Risks and follow-up

- Quality and throughput threshold numbers are reasonable defaults but untested against real corpus data — revisit when `fixtures/benchmark_translation/` is populated (issue #78).
- `ai_workstation` and `multi_node` `runtime.profile` config values are documented here but not yet wired into `config.yaml`; follow-up when those hardware tiers become active.
- Automatic embedding of `benchmark_run` metadata in `benchmark_results.json` is deferred.

items.title: perf: render via render_in + benchmark harness & continuous-perf discipline
items.body:
## Summary

Make phlex-reactive fast where it counts, and make performance **continuous** —
measured on every change, not assumed. Two halves:

**A. Hot-path fixes** (each backed by a same-machine before/after, not a guess)
**B. Measurement tooling + discipline** (benchmark harness, CI report, perf docs,
a `/perf` command, and a standing perf rule for the Claude workflow)

The headline fix: the component re-render — the hottest server path, run on every
action **and every broadcast** — went through `ActionController.renderer.render`
(ActionView's `TemplateRenderer`/`LookupContext`/log-subscriber machinery) **and**
rebuilt the off-request view context + Turbo `TagBuilder` on every call (the
comment claimed "memoized per class"; it wasn't). It now renders through
phlex-rails' lightweight `#render_in` against a genuinely memoized view context.

## Measured before/after

Pristine `main` run in an isolated `git worktree` with the **same script** as the
branch (Ruby 3.4 +YJIT, Apple Silicon, dummy app). Ratios are the point; your
absolute numbers will differ.

| Benchmark | Before | After | Delta |
|-----------|--------|-------|-------|
| `render_component` throughput | 6.99k i/s (143 us) | 14.1k i/s (71 us) | **2.0x faster** |
| `render_component` allocations | 212 obj | 99 obj | **-53%** |
| `to_stream_replace` throughput | 4.60k i/s (217 us) | 8.00k i/s (125 us) | **1.7x faster** |
| `to_stream_replace` allocations | 331 obj | 191 obj | **-42%** |
| `reactive_token` (state) allocations | 14 obj | 11 obj | -21% |
| `on(:action)` (no params) allocations | 6 obj | 5 obj | -17% |

### Honest framing (this matters)

- **The render win is largest on broadcasts.** A single change fanned out to N
  subscribers = N renders with no HTTP round trip to amortize against. There the
  2x is a real 2x.
- **At the full-request level the win washes out** — routing + middleware + token
  verify + transaction + DB dominate, so `POST /reactive/actions` throughput is
  roughly unchanged. The render optimization still removes per-render retained-
  object churn (GC pressure under load). I measured this directly and am not
  overselling it.
- The token/`on()`/regex tweaks are modest but free and correct; HMAC signing
  dominates `reactive_token`, so throughput barely moves.
- I deliberately **did not** rewrite the nested-param deep-merge for ~10% fewer
  allocations — it's correctness-critical (issues #16/#21/#24) and not the
  bottleneck. Hoisting its regex to a constant: yes. Rewriting the algorithm: no.

## What changed

**Render path (`perf(streamable)`)**
- `render_component` -> `component.render_in(memoized_view_context)`; byte-identical
  HTML, full Rails helper access (`dom_id`/`url_for`/`t`/csrf) preserved.
- View context + `TagBuilder` + `flash_builder` memoized per class, keyed on the
  renderer's identity (swap rebuilds), reset on Rails code reload
  (`config.to_prepare`). The class registry is an `ObjectSpace::WeakMap` so
  reloaded classes are GC'd, not pinned.

**Micro-opts (`perf(component)`)**
- `reactive_token` precomputes ivar symbols + state string-keys per class.
- `on(:action)` skips re-serializing an empty params hash (wire format unchanged).
- Bracket-key coercion regex hoisted to a frozen constant.
- Client: page-stable action path resolved once per controller; CSRF + pgbus
  connection id stay live (they rotate). Vendored copy re-synced.
- Bonus: the state-tamper security test is now serializer-agnostic, so it passes
  run alone or in the full suite (it relied on the Rails `_rails.data` shape).

**Tooling (`test(bench)` + `docs(perf)`)**
- `benchmark/` — micro-benches (render/token/coerce) via benchmark-ips +
  memory_profiler, and an end-to-end request bench via derailed_benchmarks.
- `rake bench` / `bench:micro` / `bench:one[name]` / `bench:request`.
- CI `bench` job: runs on every PR, uploads the report as an artifact.
  Run-and-report, **never a hard fail** (shared runners are too noisy for a
  threshold).
- `docs/performance.md`, `.claude/rules/performance.md`, `.claude/commands/perf.md`,
  plus CLAUDE.md / README / CHANGELOG updates so perf + docs are part of every PR.
- Bench gems are dev/test only — **zero new runtime dependencies** (gemspec
  untouched).

## Invariants preserved

- Signed identity, default-deny actions, schema coercion, CSRF — untouched.
- pgbus optionality — untouched (no broadcast-path behavior change).
- All existing components work verbatim (HTML byte-identical).

## Test plan

- [x] `bundle exec standardrb`
- [x] `bundle exec rspec spec/phlex spec/requests spec/generators` — 159, 0 failures
- [x] `bun test spec/javascript` — 19, 0 failures
- [x] `bundle exec rspec spec/system` (browser) — 18, 0 failures (render path +
      client change validated end-to-end, incl. focus preservation + rapid-click race)
- [x] `rake bench:micro` / `rake bench:request` run clean and produce the report
- New: `spec/phlex/reactive/streamable_view_context_spec.rb` (memoization,
  renderer-swap invalidation, byte-identical output, `render_in` helper access)

items.title: Add benchmark lookup tables comparing fast58 to bs58 in README
items.body:
### Motivation
- Provide an easy-to-read lookup table that compares `fast58` throughput to the npm `bs58` baseline using exact measured numbers from the benchmark harness. 
- Surface both suite-level geometric means and per-payload-size results so readers can quickly assess relative performance across common workloads.

### Description
- Added a new "Benchmark lookup table (fast58 vs npm `bs58`)" section to `README.md` containing suite-level winners and gmean ops/s for Broad Mix, 32B, 64B, and Large Payloads. 
- Included a detailed per-size table for Broad Mix (0B through 256B) showing exact encode/decode throughput for `fast58 js current` and `bs58` and computed ratios. 
- Recorded the measurement date and the command used to produce the numbers (`bun run benchmark.ts`).
- Only `README.md` was modified to add the lookup tables and associated descriptive text.

### Testing
- Ran the benchmark harness with `bun run benchmark.ts` and used the reported throughput values to populate the tables, and the command completed successfully.
- No other automated tests were changed or required for this documentation update.
